translations.literal: Wang Yingxiong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingxiong

sentences.zh: 王應熊，字非熊，巴縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Yingxiong, style name Feixiong, was a native of Baxian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingxiong, whose style name was Feixiong, came from Baxian.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，歷官詹事，以憂歸。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he served successively as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then returned home on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tianqi emperor he rose to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent before retiring to mourn a parent.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，召拜禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongzhen he was recalled and made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，帝遣宦官出守邊鎮，應熊上言：「陛下焦勞求治，何一不倚信群臣，乃群臣不肯任勞任怨，致陛下萬不獲已，權遣近侍監理。

translations.literal: The next winter the emperor dispatched eunuchs to garrison the frontier posts. Yingxiong memorialized: "Your Majesty toils in anxiety seeking good governance—what matter do you not entrust to your ministers? Yet the ministers are unwilling to bear hardship and accept blame, forcing Your Majesty, when utterly without alternative, to provisionally send intimate attendants to oversee affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter the emperor sent eunuchs to take charge of the border garrisons. Yingxiong submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty labors tirelessly to bring order to the realm and relies on your ministers in every respect; yet because they refuse to shoulder hardship and blame, you have been driven, with no other choice, to dispatch your close attendants to supervise affairs on a provisional basis.

sentences.zh: 書之青史，謂有聖明不世出之主，而群工不克仰承，直當愧死。

translations.literal: Recorded in the green annals, it will be said that there was a sagely and enlightened sovereign unequaled in his age, while the host of officials could not look up and carry out his will—they ought simply to die of shame.
translations.idiomatic: When this is written into history, posterity will say that a sage emperor without peer had ministers who could not rise to his trust; they ought to die of shame.

sentences.zh: 且自神宗以來，士習人心不知職掌何事，有舉《會典》律例告之者，反訝為申、韓刑名。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the Shenzong reign scholarly habit and popular sentiment have not known what duties they hold; when someone cites the Statutes and Regulations of the Administrative Compendium, others are instead astonished, taking it for the penal nomenclature of Shen Buhai and Han Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shenzong's day scholars and officials have lost sight of their proper duties; cite the Administrative Compendium or the code of statutes and you are met with surprise, as though you were preaching the harsh legalism of Shen Buhai and Han Fei.

sentences.zh: 近日諸臣之病，非臨事不擔當之故，乃平時未講求之過也；

translations.literal: The recent ailment of the ministers is not that they fail to take responsibility when affairs arise, but that in ordinary times they have not studied and sought understanding;
translations.idiomatic: The fault of today's ministers lies not in refusing responsibility at the moment of crisis, but in failing to study their duties in quieter times;

sentences.zh: 亦非因循於夙習之故，實愆忘於舊章之過也。」

translations.literal: nor is it that they follow old habits, but truly that they have transgressed through forgetting the old regulations."
translations.idiomatic: nor is it mere habit and inertia, but a real neglect of established precedent."

sentences.zh: 語皆迎帝意，遂蒙眷註。

translations.literal: His words all pleased the emperor's mind, and he thereupon received special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Every line flattered the emperor's views, and he won the throne's special favor.

sentences.zh: 嘗酗酒，詬尚書黃汝良，為給事中馮元飆所劾，汝良為之隱，乃解。

translations.literal: Once, drunk, he reviled Minister Huang Ruliang; he was impeached by Supervising Secretary Feng Yuanbiao, but Ruliang concealed the matter for him, and the case was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion, drunk, he abused Minister Huang Ruliang. Supervising Secretary Feng Yuanbiao impeached him, but Huang covered for him and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 五年，進左侍郎，元飆發其貪汙狀，帝不省。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Left Vice Minister; Yuanbiao exposed his corrupt conduct, but the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Left Vice Minister. Yuanbiao laid out evidence of his corruption, but the emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 應熊博學多才，熟諳典故，而性谿刻強很，人多畏之。

translations.literal: Yingxiong was broadly learned and richly talented, thoroughly versed in precedent, yet by nature narrow, harsh, and obstinate, and many feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiong was learned and capable, with a deep command of precedent, but he was narrow, harsh, and unyielding by nature, and many stood in fear of him.

sentences.zh: 周延儒、溫體仁援以自助，鹹與親善。

translations.literal: Zhou Yanru and Wen Tiren drew on him to help themselves, and all were on friendly terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yanru and Wen Tiren enlisted him as an ally, and both cultivated close ties with him.

sentences.zh: 及延儒罷，體仁援益力。

translations.literal: When Yanru was dismissed, Tiren's support for him grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanru fell from power, Tiren backed him all the more vigorously.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，廷推閣臣，應熊望輕不與，特旨擢禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，與何吾騶並入參機務。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year, at the court recommendation for Grand Secretaries, Yingxiong's standing was slight and he was not included; by special edict he was promoted to Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering with He Wuyao to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the court nominated candidates for the Grand Secretariat; Yingxiong's reputation was too slight to make the list, yet a special edict raised him to Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, and he entered the privy council alongside He Wuyao.

sentences.zh: 命下，朝野胥駭。

translations.literal: When the order was issued, court and countryside alike were appalled.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was announced, the whole realm was stunned.

sentences.zh: 給事中章正宸劾之曰：「應熊強愎自張，縱橫為習，小才足覆短，小辨足濟貪，今大用，必且芟除異己，報復恩仇，混淆毀譽。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Zhenchen impeached him, saying: "Yingxiong is obstinate and self-aggrandizing, practiced in manipulation; petty talent suffices to cover his faults, petty eloquence to feed his greed. Now that he is greatly employed, he will surely weed out those unlike himself, repay favors and avenge grudges, and confound praise and blame.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Zhenchen impeached him: "Yingxiong is stubborn and overbearing, skilled in intrigue; a little talent hides his faults and a little eloquence serves his greed. Give him high office and he will purge rivals, settle scores, and twist reputation to his ends.

sentences.zh: 況狼籍封靡，淪於市行。

translations.literal: Moreover he is dissolute and extravagant, fallen to the ways of the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He is dissolute and extravagant, no better than a market hustler.

sentences.zh: 願收還成命，別選忠良。

translations.literal: I pray that the completed order be withdrawn and another loyal and worthy man be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to revoke the appointment and choose a worthy man instead.

sentences.zh: 且訛言謂左右先容，由他途以進，使天下薰心捷足之徒馳騁而起，為聖德累不小。」

translations.literal: Moreover slander says that those at the emperor's side paved the way and that he advanced by another route, so that throughout the realm those whose hearts are tainted and whose feet are swift will gallop forth—no small burden on sagely virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Rumor moreover says court favorites smoothed his path and that he rose by back channels, encouraging every schemer in the land to rush forward—a grave stain on Your Majesty's virtue."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，下正宸詔獄，削籍歸。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, sent Zhenchen to the imperial prison by edict, and stripped him of registry and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, had Zhenchen thrown into the imperial prison, struck him from the rolls, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 有勸應熊為文彥博者，應熊咈然，佯具疏引退，語多憤激。

translations.literal: Some urged Yingxiong to play the part of Wen Yanbo; he snorted in displeasure, pretended to draft a memorial withdrawing, and his language was much embittered.
translations.idiomatic: Some advised him to emulate the magnanimous statesman Wen Yanbo; he snorted in annoyance, feigned a resignation memorial, and wrote in bitter, angry tones.

sentences.zh: 屢為給事中範淑泰、御史吳履中所攻，帝皆不問。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly attacked by Supervising Secretary Fan Shutai and Censor Wu Lüzhong, but the emperor in every case paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Fan Shutai and Censor Wu Lüzhong attacked him again and again, but the emperor ignored every charge.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，流賊陷鳳陽，毀皇陵。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year, bandits took Fengyang and destroyed the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year rebel armies captured Fengyang and desecrated the imperial mausoleums.

sentences.zh: 巡撫楊一鵬，應熊座主；

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Yang Yipeng was Yingxiong's chief examiner;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Yang Yipeng had been Yingxiong's chief examiner;

sentences.zh: 巡按吳振纓，體仁姻也。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Wu Zhenying was related to Tiren by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Wu Zhenying was Wen Tiren's kinsman by marriage.

sentences.zh: 二人恐帝震怒，留一鵬、振纓疏未上，俟恢復報同奏之，遂擬旨令撫按戴罪。

translations.literal: The two men feared the emperor's wrath, withheld Yipeng's and Zhenying's memorials, and waited to submit them together with a recovery report; they then drafted an edict ordering the coordinator and censor to retain their posts while bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the emperor's wrath, the two held back Yipeng's and Zhenying's reports until they could file a recovery notice with them, then drafted an edict letting the coordinator and censor keep office while bearing guilt.

sentences.zh: 主事鄭爾說、胡江交章詆應熊、體仁朋比誤國，帝怒謫二人，而給事中何楷、許譽卿、範淑泰，御史張纘曾、吳履中、張肯堂言之不已。

translations.literal: Section Heads Zheng Ershuo and Hu Jiang submitted successive memorials denouncing Yingxiong and Tiren for factional collusion that harmed the state; the emperor in anger demoted the two, while Supervising Secretaries He Kai, Xu Yuqing, and Fan Shutai and Censors Zhang Zuanzeng, Wu Lüzhong, and Zhang Kentang spoke without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Section Heads Zheng Ershuo and Hu Jiang memorialized in turn accusing Yingxiong and Tiren of factional collusion that ruined the state. The emperor angrily demoted the two memorialists, but Supervising Secretaries He Kai, Xu Yuqing, and Fan Shutai and Censors Zhang Zuanzeng, Wu Lüzhong, and Zhang Kentang kept pressing the case.

sentences.zh: 淑泰言：「一鵬《恢復疏》以正月二十一日，《核察失事情形疏》以正月二十八日，天下有未失事先恢復者哉？

translations.literal: Shutai said: "Yipeng's 'Recovery Memorial' is dated the twenty-first day of the first month, and his 'Memorial on Investigating the Circumstances of the Loss' the twenty-eighth—under heaven is there anyone who recovers before he has lost?
translations.idiomatic: Shutai wrote: "Yipeng's 'Recovery Memorial' is dated the twenty-first of the first month and his 'Memorial Investigating the Loss' the twenty-eighth—who in the world reports recovery before the disaster has even occurred?

sentences.zh: 應熊改填月日，欺誑之罪難辭。」

translations.literal: Yingxiong altered and filled in the month and day; the crime of deception is hard to escape."
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiong altered the dates on the documents—a charge of fraud he cannot evade."

sentences.zh: 且劾其他受賄事。

translations.literal: He also impeached him on other matters of taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He also accused him of other acts of bribery.

sentences.zh: 帝顧應熊厚，皆不聽，而鐫楷、纘曾秩，慰諭應熊。

translations.literal: The emperor, looking on Yingxiong with favor, would not heed any of it, but reduced Kai's and Zuanzeng's ranks and comforted Yingxiong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Yingxiong and rejected every charge, demoting He Kai and Zhang Zuanzeng instead while reassuring Yingxiong.

sentences.zh: 應熊亦屢疏辯，謂：「座主門生，誼不容薄，敢辭比之名。

translations.literal: Yingxiong also repeatedly memorialized in his defense, saying: "Between chief examiner and student, duty does not permit slighting; I dare reject the name of factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiong defended himself in repeated memorials: "Between examiner and student the bond of duty forbids neglect—I cannot accept the label of factional collusion.

sentences.zh: 票擬實臣起草，敢辭誤之罪。」

translations.literal: The draft rescript was in truth composed by me; I dare reject the crime of error."
translations.idiomatic: I myself drafted the rescript; I cannot deny responsibility for the mistake."

sentences.zh: 楷益憤，屢疏糾之，最後復疏言：「故事，奏章非發抄，外人無由聞；

translations.literal: Kai grew still angrier, repeatedly memorialized to impeach him, and finally memorialized again, saying: "By precedent, unless a memorial is issued for copying, outsiders have no means to hear of it;
translations.idiomatic: Kai grew angrier still and impeached him again and again. At last he wrote: "By precedent a memorial cannot be known outside the court unless it is released for copying;

sentences.zh: 非奉旨，邸報不許抄傳。

translations.literal: unless there is an imperial order, the Court Gazette may not be copied and transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: without an imperial order the Court Gazette may not circulate it.

sentences.zh: 臣疏六月初十日上，十四日始奉明旨，應熊乃於十三日奏辯，旨尚未下，應熊何由知？

translations.literal: My memorial was submitted on the tenth day of the sixth month; only on the fourteenth did I receive the clear imperial order. Yet Yingxiong on the thirteenth submitted his defense—the order had not yet been issued; how could Yingxiong have known?
translations.idiomatic: I submitted my memorial on the tenth of the sixth month and received the imperial response only on the fourteenth. Yingxiong filed his defense on the thirteenth, before the order was issued—how could he have known?

sentences.zh: 臣不解者一。

translations.literal: This is the first thing your servant does not understand.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first thing I cannot understand.

sentences.zh: 且旨下必由六科抄發。

translations.literal: Moreover when an order is issued it must pass through the Six Offices for Scrutiny to be copied and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover every edict must be copied and released through the Six Offices for Scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 臣疏十四日下，而百戶趙光修先送錦衣堂上官，則疏可不由科抄矣。

translations.literal: My memorial was issued on the fourteenth, yet Company Commander Zhao Guangxiu first delivered it to the senior officer of the Brocade Guard—so the memorial could bypass the Offices' copying.
translations.idiomatic: My memorial was issued on the fourteenth, yet Company Commander Zhao Guangxiu had already delivered it to the Brocade Guard—so the memorial need not pass through the Offices at all.

sentences.zh: 臣不解者二。」

translations.literal: This is the second thing your servant does not understand."
translations.idiomatic: That is the second thing I cannot understand."

sentences.zh: 應熊始懼，具疏引罪。

translations.literal: Only then did Yingxiong begin to fear; he fully memorialized accepting guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Yingxiong grow afraid and submit a full confession.

sentences.zh: 帝下其家人及直日中書七人於獄。

translations.literal: The emperor sent his household members and seven secretaries on duty in the Grand Secretariat to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor imprisoned his household staff and seven secretaries on duty in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 獄具，家人戍邊，中書貶二秩。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, the household members were banished to the frontier and the secretaries were demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: After the trial the household servants were exiled to the frontier and the secretaries demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 應熊乃屢疏乞休去，乘傳賜道里費，行人護行。

translations.literal: Yingxiong then repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; he was granted post-horses, traveling expenses, and an envoy to escort him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiong repeatedly asked to retire. He was given relay horses, traveling funds, and an imperial messenger to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 帝亦知應熊不協人望，特己所拔擢，不欲以人言去也。

translations.literal: The emperor also knew that Yingxiong did not accord with popular expectation, but since he was one the emperor himself had raised up, he did not wish to remove him because of men's words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Yingxiong lacked public support, but because he had personally elevated him he was unwilling to dismiss him on rumor alone.

sentences.zh: 十二年遣官存問。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year officials were dispatched to inquire after his welfare.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the court sent officials to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 其弟應熙橫於鄉，鄉人詣闕擊登聞鼓，列狀至四百八十余條，贓一百七十余萬，詞連應熊。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yingxi tyrannized the countryside; villagers went to the capital and struck the Denunciation Drum, listing more than four hundred and eighty charges and bribes of more than 1.7 million, with language implicating Yingxiong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yingxi terrorized the countryside until locals went to the capital and beat the Denunciation Drum, filing more than four hundred eighty accusations involving over 1.7 million in bribes and implicating Yingxiong.

sentences.zh: 詔下撫按勘究。

translations.literal: An edict was issued ordering the coordinator and censor to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the provincial authorities to investigate.

sentences.zh: 會應熊復召，事得解。

translations.literal: It happened that Yingxiong was summoned again, and the matter was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingxiong was summoned back to court the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時延儒再相，患言者攻己，獨念應熊剛很，可藉以制之，力言於帝。

translations.literal: At that time Yanru was again chief minister; vexed that critics attacked him, he alone thought that Yingxiong's obstinate harshness could be used to restrain them, and he spoke forcefully to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru was chief minister again and, harassed by critics, decided that Yingxiong's harsh stubbornness could be used to silence them; he pressed the point hard with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，遣行人召應熊。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year an imperial messenger was sent to summon Yingxiong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the court dispatched an envoy to recall Yingxiong.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，應熊未至，延儒已罷歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year, before Yingxiong arrived, Yanru had already been dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth month of the following year Yingxiong had not yet arrived and Yanru had already been dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 給事中龔鼎孳密疏言：「陛下召應熊，必因其秉國之日，眾口交攻，以為孤立無黨；

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Gong Dingzi submitted a secret memorial, saying: "Your Majesty summons Yingxiong surely because, during his tenure of state, all mouths attacked him and he was thought isolated and without faction;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Gong Dingzi wrote a secret memorial: "Your Majesty recalls Yingxiong because, when he held office, critics attacked him from every side and he seemed isolated and factionless;

sentences.zh: 孰知其同年密契，肺腑深聯，恃延儒在也。

translations.literal: who would know that he and Yanru were close classmates, joined heart and lung, relying on Yanru's presence?
translations.idiomatic: yet who knows that he and Yanru were classmates bound heart to heart, and that he counted on Yanru's backing?

sentences.zh: 臣去年入都，聞應熊賄延儒為再召計。

translations.literal: Your servant last year entered the capital and heard that Yingxiong bribed Yanru to plan his recall.
translations.idiomatic: When I reached the capital last year I heard that Yingxiong had bribed Yanru to arrange his recall.

sentences.zh: 延儒對眾大言，至尊欲起巴縣。

translations.literal: Yanru declared before the multitude in loud voice that the Sovereign wished to raise up the man from Baxian.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru announced publicly that the Sovereign meant to recall the man from Baxian.

sentences.zh: 巴縣者，應熊也。

translations.literal: The man from Baxian was Yingxiong.
translations.idiomatic: The man from Baxian was Yingxiong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召命果下。

translations.literal: Before long the summons was indeed issued.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the summons came down as he had said.

sentences.zh: 以政本重地，私相援引，是延儒雖去猶未去，天下事何堪再誤！」

translations.literal: To use this weighty seat of government for private mutual advancement—though Yanru has gone, he is as yet not gone; how can affairs under heaven bear to be mistaken again!"
translations.idiomatic: To fill this weighty post through private patronage means Yanru is gone in name but not in power—how can the realm endure another such mistake!"

sentences.zh: 帝得疏心動，留未下。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the memorial his heart was moved; he kept it and did not issue it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shaken by the memorial and withheld it without acting.

sentences.zh: 已而延儒被逮，不即赴，俟應熊至，始尾之行。

translations.literal: Before long Yanru was arrested; he did not go at once but waited until Yingxiong arrived, then followed at the tail of the procession.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanru was arrested he did not go at once but waited until Yingxiong arrived and only then set out behind him.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝顧中官曰：「延儒何久不至？」

translations.literal: One day the emperor turned to the eunuchs and said: "Why is Yanru so long in coming?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor asked his eunuchs: "Why is Yanru taking so long to arrive?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「需王應熊先入耳。」

translations.literal: They answered: "He is waiting for Wang Yingxiong to enter the capital first."
translations.idiomatic: They replied: "He is waiting for Wang Yingxiong to reach the capital first."

sentences.zh: 帝益疑之。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still more suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's suspicions deepened.

sentences.zh: 九月，應熊至，宿朝房。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Yingxiong arrived and lodged in the court lodging house.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yingxiong arrived and stayed in the court lodging quarters.

sentences.zh: 請入對，不許；

translations.literal: He requested an audience and was not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: He asked for an audience and was refused;

sentences.zh: 請歸田，許之，乃慚沮而返。

translations.literal: he requested to return to his fields and was allowed; he then returned in shame and dejection.
translations.idiomatic: he asked to retire to his estate and was allowed to do so, and went home in shame and dismay.

sentences.zh: 十七年三月，京師陷。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventeenth year the capital fell to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 五月，福王立於南京。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 八月，張獻忠陷四川。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Zhang Xianzhong took Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhang Xianzhong overran Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 乃改應熊兵部尚書兼文淵閣大學士，總督川、湖、雲、貴軍務，專辦川寇。

translations.literal: Yingxiong was then transferred to Minister of War and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth, with overall command of military affairs in Sichuan, Huguang, Yunnan, and Guizhou, charged specifically with handling the Sichuan bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxiong was then made Minister of War and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth, with overall command of military affairs in Sichuan, Huguang, Yunnan, and Guizhou, charged specifically with suppressing the Sichuan rebels.

sentences.zh: 時川中諸郡，惟遵義未下，應熊入守之，縞素誓師，開幕府，傳檄討賊。

translations.literal: At that time among the prefectures of Sichuan only Zunyi had not fallen; Yingxiong entered to defend it, swore the army in white mourning dress, opened a field headquarters, and issued proclamations to campaign against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Of all Sichuan only Zunyi still held out. Yingxiong entered to defend it, swore his troops in white, opened a field headquarters, and issued proclamations calling for the rebels' destruction.

sentences.zh: 明年奏上方略，請敕川陜、湖貴兩總督，鄖陽、湖廣、貴州、雲南四巡撫出師合討，並劾四川巡撫馬體乾縱兵淫掠，革職提問。

translations.literal: The next year he memorialized his strategy, requesting imperial orders to the two supreme commanders of Shaanxi-Sichuan and Huguang-Guizhou and the four grand coordinators of Xiangyang, Huguang, Guizhou, and Yunnan to march in joint campaign, and also impeached Sichuan Grand Coordinator Ma Tigan for letting his troops run wild in plunder, stripping him of office and summoning him for trial.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he submitted his strategy, asking the throne to order the two regional commanders of Shaanxi-Sichuan and Huguang-Guizhou and the four grand coordinators of Xiangyang, Huguang, Guizhou, and Yunnan to launch a joint offensive, and impeached Sichuan Grand Coordinator Ma Tigan for allowing his troops to loot and ravage, stripping him of office for trial.

sentences.zh: 命未達而南都亡，雲乾居職如故。

translations.literal: The order had not arrived when the Southern Capital perished; Tigan remained in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before the order arrived the Southern Capital fell, and Ma Tigan kept his post unchanged.

sentences.zh: 已而獻忠死，諸將楊展等各據州縣自雄，應熊不能制。

translations.literal: Before long Xianzhong died, and the generals Yang Zhan and others each held prefectures and counties and made themselves strong; Yingxiong could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhong's death generals such as Yang Zhan seized prefectures and counties and ruled as petty warlords, and Yingxiong could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 其部將曾英最有功，復重慶，屢破賊兵。

translations.literal: His subordinate general Zeng Ying achieved the most merit, recovered Chongqing, and repeatedly defeated bandit troops.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Zeng Ying won the greatest distinction, recovered Chongqing, and repeatedly routed rebel forces.

sentences.zh: 王祥亦出師綦江相犄角。

translations.literal: Wang Xiang also marched out from Qijiang to form a pincer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang also marched from Qijiang to support him in a pincer movement.

sentences.zh: 祥才武不及英，而應熊委任過之。

translations.literal: Xiang's talent and martial prowess did not match Ying's, yet Yingxiong entrusted him beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang was less capable than Zeng Ying, yet Yingxiong favored him above the better man.

sentences.zh: 又明年十月，獻忠余黨孫可望、李定國等南走重慶，英戰歿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year, Xianzhong's remnant followers Sun Kewang, Li Dingguo, and others fled south toward Chongqing; Ying died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the next year Xianzhong's followers Sun Kewang and Li Dingguo marched south on Chongqing, and Zeng Ying was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 可望襲破遵義，應熊遁入永寧山中，旋卒於畢節衛。

translations.literal: Kewang stormed and took Zunyi; Yingxiong fled into the Yongning mountains and soon died at Bijie Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Kewang stormed Zunyi; Yingxiong fled into the Yongning hills and soon died at Bijie.

sentences.zh: 一子陽禧，死於兵，竟無後。

translations.literal: He had one son, Yangxi, who died in the fighting; in the end he left no heir.
translations.idiomatic: His only son Yangxi died in the fighting, and he left no descendants.

sentences.zh: 何吾騶，香山人。

translations.literal: He Wuyao was a native of Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuyao came from Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十七年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the forty-seventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士歷官少詹事。

translations.literal: From Hanlin Bachelor he served successively up to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as a Hanlin Bachelor he rose to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年，擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongzhen he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongzhen he was made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六年十一月，加尚書，同王應熊入閣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixth year he was made Minister and entered the cabinet together with Wang Yingxiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the sixth year he was raised to ministerial rank and entered the Grand Secretariat alongside Wang Yingxiong.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁久柄政，欲斥給事中許譽卿。

translations.literal: Wen Tiren had long held power and wished to drive out Supervising Secretary Xu Yuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren had dominated the government for years and sought to oust Supervising Secretary Xu Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 已擬旨，文震孟爭之，吾騶亦助為言。

translations.literal: An edict had already been drafted, but Wen Zhenmeng contested it and Wuyao also spoke in support.
translations.idiomatic: The rescript had already been drafted when Wen Zhenmeng objected, and Wuyao added his voice in support.

sentences.zh: 體仁訐奏，帝奪震孟官，兼罷吾騶。

translations.literal: Tiren lodged an accusatory memorial; the emperor stripped Zhenmeng of office and also dismissed Wuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren filed a denunciatory memorial, and the emperor stripped Zhenmeng of office and dismissed Wuyao as well.

sentences.zh: 詳見《震孟傳》。

translations.literal: For details see the biography of Wen Zhenmeng.
translations.idiomatic: For details see the biography of Wen Zhenmeng.

sentences.zh: 居久之，唐王自立於福州，召為首輔，與鄭芝龍議事輒相牴牾。

translations.literal: After a long interval the Prince of Tang established himself at Fuzhou and summoned him as chief minister; in deliberations with Zheng Zhilong they constantly clashed.
translations.idiomatic: After some time the Prince of Tang set up court at Fuzhou and made him chief minister, but he and Zheng Zhilong clashed repeatedly over policy.

sentences.zh: 閩疆既失，踉蹌回廣州。

translations.literal: Once Fujian was lost he made his way back to Guangzhou in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: When Fujian fell he fled in disorder back to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永明王以原官召之，為給事中金堡、大理寺少卿趙昱等所攻。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yongming summoned him at his former rank, but he was attacked by Supervising Secretary Jin Bao, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Zhao Yu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yongming recalled him to his former post, but Supervising Secretary Jin Bao, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Zhao Yu, and others attacked him.

sentences.zh: 引疾辭去，卒於家。

translations.literal: He resigned citing illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 張至發

translations.literal: Zhang Zhifa
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhifa

sentences.zh: 張至發，淄川人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhifa was a native of Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhifa came from Zichuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the twenty-ninth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知玉田、遵化。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Yutian and Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Yutian and then of Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 行取，授禮部主事，改御史。

translations.literal: Selected for capital office, he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Rites and then transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for service in the capital, he became a secretary in the Ministry of Rites and was later made a censor.

sentences.zh: 時齊、楚、浙三黨方熾，至發，齊黨也，上疏陳內降之弊。

translations.literal: At that time the Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions were in full blaze; Zhifa belonged to the Qi faction and memorialized on the abuses of inner edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions were then at their height; Zhifa, a Qi man, memorialized against the abuse of edicts issued from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 因言：「陛下惡結黨，而秉揆者先不能超然門戶外。

translations.literal: He said: "Your Majesty hates faction, yet those who hold the chief ministership cannot first stand outside party gates themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Your Majesty detests factionalism, yet the chief ministers cannot themselves stand above party lines.

sentences.zh: 頃讀科臣疏云：『日來慰諭輔臣溫旨，輔臣與司禮自相參定，方聽禦批。』

translations.literal: Recently reading a supervising secretary's memorial: 'Of late the comforting edicts to the chief ministers are settled between the ministers and the Directorate of Ceremonial before the imperial rescript is heard.'
translations.idiomatic: He cited a supervising secretary's memorial: 'Lately the reassuring edicts to the chief ministers are agreed between the ministers and the Directorate of Ceremonial before the imperial rescript is issued.'

sentences.zh: 果若人言，天下事尚可問耶？」

translations.literal: If this is truly so, can affairs under heaven still be questioned?
translations.idiomatic: If that is true, can the affairs of the realm still be entrusted to them?"

sentences.zh: 語皆刺葉向高，帝不報。

translations.literal: His words all stabbed at Ye Xianggao; the emperor made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Every line was aimed at Ye Xianggao; the emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 時言官爭排東林，戶部郎中李樸不平，抗疏爭。

translations.literal: At that time censors vied to attack the Donglin faction; Section Head Li Pu was indignant and submitted a bold memorial in protest.
translations.idiomatic: Censors were then competing to attack the Donglin faction; Section Head Li Pu submitted a forceful memorial in protest.

sentences.zh: 至發遂劾樸背公死黨，誑語欺君，帝亦不報。

translations.literal: Zhifa thereupon impeached Pu for betraying the public and dying for faction, with deceitful words that misled the ruler; the emperor again made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifa then impeached Pu for betraying the public interest and clinging to faction, with deceitful words that misled the throne; again the emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 尋出按河南。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as investigating censor in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as investigating censor in Henan.

sentences.zh: 福王之藩洛陽，中使相望於道。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu took up his fief at Luoyang, palace envoys lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu went to his fief at Luoyang, palace envoys thronged the route.

sentences.zh: 至發以禮裁之，無敢橫。

translations.literal: Zhifa restrained them by ritual, and none dared act arrogantly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifa held them to proper ritual, and none dared abuse his authority.

sentences.zh: 宗祿不給，為置義田，以贍貧者。

translations.literal: When stipends for the imperial clan were not paid, he set up charitable fields to support the poor.
translations.idiomatic: When clan stipends went unpaid, he established charitable fields to support the needy.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，豫省饑，請留餉備振，又請改折漕糧，皆報聞。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, when Henan suffered famine, he requested that grain reserves be kept for relief and that tribute grain be converted to cash payment; both were approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year, during famine in Henan, he asked to retain grain reserves for relief and to convert tribute grain to cash payments; both requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 還朝，引病歸。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he cited illness and went home.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，進大理寺丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi he was made vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 三年請終養。

translations.literal: In the third year he requested to complete mourning for his parent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he asked leave to complete mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢黨薦之，矯旨令吏部擢用，至發方養親不出。

translations.literal: The eunuch faction recommended him; a forged edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel to promote him, but Zhifa was caring for his parent and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian's faction recommended him and a forged edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel to promote him, but Zhifa was in mourning and refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年，起順天府丞，進光祿卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongzhen he was recalled as vice minister of Shuntian Prefecture and promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongzhen he was recalled as vice minister of Shuntian Prefecture and promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 精核積弊，多所厘正，遂受帝知。

translations.literal: He thoroughly investigated accumulated abuses and corrected many of them, and thus won the emperor's trust.
translations.idiomatic: He rigorously investigated long-standing abuses and corrected many of them, winning the emperor's confidence.

sentences.zh: 八年春，遷刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year he was made Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝將增置閣臣，以翰林不習世務，思用他官參之，召廷臣數十人，各授一疏，令擬旨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the emperor intended to add Grand Secretaries; because Hanlin scholars were unversed in practical affairs, he thought to include other officials, summoned several dozen courtiers, and gave each a memorial to draft a rescript.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor planned to add Grand Secretaries; finding Hanlin scholars unversed in practical administration, he summoned dozens of officials, gave each a memorial, and ordered them to draft rescripts.

sentences.zh: 遂擢至發禮部左侍郎兼東閣大學士，與文震孟同入直。

translations.literal: Zhifa was thereupon promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering duty together with Wen Zhenmeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the privy council alongside Wen Zhenmeng.

sentences.zh: 自世宗朝許贊後，外僚入閣，自至發始。

translations.literal: Since Xu Zan in the Jiajing reign, this was the first time an outside official entered the cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xu Zan under Jiajing, he was the first outside official to enter the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時溫體仁為首輔，錢士升、王應熊、何吾騶次之。

translations.literal: At that time Wen Tiren was chief minister, with Qian Shisheng, Wang Yingxiong, and He Wuyao next.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren was then chief minister, followed by Qian Shisheng, Wang Yingxiong, and He Wuyao.

sentences.zh: 越二年，體仁輩盡去，至發遂為首輔。

translations.literal: Two years later, when Tiren and the others had all gone, Zhifa became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, when Tiren and the others had all left office, Zhifa became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，申時行、王錫爵先後柄政，大旨相紹述，謂之「傳衣缽」。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period Shen Shixing and Wang Xijue had successively held power; their great principles were passed on in succession, called 'transmitting the robe and bowl.'
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli, Shen Shixing and Wang Xijue had held power in turn, passing on a single line of policy known as 'transmitting the robe and bowl.'

sentences.zh: 至發代體仁，一切守其所為，而才智機變遜之，以位次居首，非帝之所註也。

translations.literal: Zhifa replaced Tiren and kept everything Tiren had done, but his talent, wisdom, and adaptability fell short; occupying the first place though not the emperor's favorite.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifa succeeded Tiren and preserved all his policies, but lacked his wit and flexibility; he held first rank without enjoying the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 嘗簡東宮講官，擯黃道周，為給事中馮元飆所刺。

translations.literal: Once, in selecting lecturers for the Eastern Palace, he excluded Huang Daozhou and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Feng Yuanbiao.
translations.idiomatic: When selecting lecturers for the Eastern Palace he excluded Huang Daozhou, drawing impeachment from Supervising Secretary Feng Yuanbiao.

sentences.zh: 至發怒，兩疏詆道周，而極頌體仁孤執不欺，復為編修吳偉業所劾。

translations.literal: Zhifa in anger submitted two memorials denouncing Daozhou while lavishly praising Tiren's solitary integrity and honesty, and was again impeached by Compiler Wu Weiye.
translations.idiomatic: In anger Zhifa submitted two memorials attacking Daozhou while praising Tiren's solitary integrity, and was impeached again by Compiler Wu Weiye.

sentences.zh: 講官項煜論至發把持考選，庇兒女姻任浚而抑成勇。

translations.literal: Lecturer Xiang Yu charged that Zhifa controlled examinations and appointments, shielding his son-in-law Ren Jun while suppressing Cheng Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturer Xiang Yu accused Zhifa of controlling examinations and appointments, favoring his son-in-law Ren Jun while suppressing Cheng Yong.

sentences.zh: 至發上章辯，帝遂逐煜去。

translations.literal: Zhifa memorialized in defense; the emperor thereupon drove Yu out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifa defended himself in a memorial, and the emperor dismissed Yu.

sentences.zh: 內閣中書黃應恩悍戾，體仁、至發輩倚任之，恃勢恣橫。

translations.literal: Within the Grand Secretariat, Secretary Huang Ying'en was fierce and overbearing; Tiren, Zhifa, and others relied on him, and he abused his power.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretariat Secretary Huang Ying'en was violent and overbearing; Tiren and Zhifa relied on him, and he abused his power at will.

sentences.zh: 及為正字，不當復為東宮侍書，恐帝與太子開講同日也。

translations.literal: When made Correcting Writer he ought not again to serve as Eastern Palace calligrapher, lest the emperor and crown prince hold lectures on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: As Correcting Writer he should not also serve as Eastern Palace calligrapher, lest the emperor and crown prince lecture on the same day.

sentences.zh: 至發不諳故事，令兼之。

translations.literal: Zhifa did not know precedent and ordered him to hold both posts.
translations.idiomatic: Unfamiliar with precedent, Zhifa ordered him to hold both posts.

sentences.zh: 應恩不能兼，講官撰講義送應恩繕錄，拒不納。

translations.literal: Ying'en could not manage both; when lecturers sent lecture drafts for him to copy, he refused to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to manage both, Ying'en refused to copy lecture drafts sent by the lecturers.

sentences.zh: 檢討楊士聰論之，至發揭寢其疏，士聰復上書閣中，極論其事，至發終庇之。

translations.literal: Reviewer Yang Shicong criticized this; Zhifa suppressed his memorial, and when Shicong wrote again to the Grand Secretariat, Zhifa still shielded Ying'en.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewer Yang Shicong criticized this; Zhifa suppressed his memorial, and when Shicong wrote again to the secretariat Zhifa still protected Ying'en.

sentences.zh: 會復故總督楊鶴官，許給誥命，應恩當撰文。

translations.literal: It happened that former supreme commander Yang He was restored to office and was to receive an edict of appointment; Ying'en was to draft the text.
translations.idiomatic: When former supreme commander Yang He was restored and was to receive an edict of appointment, Ying'en was to draft the text.

sentences.zh: 因其子嗣昌得君，力為洗雪。

translations.literal: Because his son Sichang had the emperor's favor, he worked hard to whitewash Yang He.
translations.idiomatic: Because his son Sichang enjoyed imperial favor, he worked hard to clear Yang He's name.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，將加罪，至發擬公揭救。

translations.literal: This defied the imperial will and was to be punished; Zhifa drafted a joint memorial to save him.
translations.idiomatic: This offended the throne and was to be punished; Zhifa drafted a joint memorial in his defense.

sentences.zh: 同官孔貞運、傅冠曰：「曩許士柔事，吾輩未嘗救，獨救應恩何也？」

translations.literal: His colleagues Kong Zhenyun and Fu Guan said: "In the matter of Xu Shirou before, we never intervened—why save Ying'en alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues Kong Zhenyun and Fu Guan said: "In Xu Shirou's case we never intervened—why save Ying'en alone?"

sentences.zh: 至發咈然曰：「公等不救，我自救之。」

translations.literal: Zhifa snorted and said: "If you gentlemen will not save him, I will save him myself."
translations.idiomatic: Zhifa retorted: "If you will not save him, I will."

sentences.zh: 連上三揭。

translations.literal: He submitted three joint memorials in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three joint memorials in succession.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，特降諭削應恩籍，嗣昌疏救，亦不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen and specially issued an edict stripping Ying'en from the rolls; Sichang memorialized in his defense, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and issued a special edict striking Ying'en from the rolls; Sichang memorialized in his defense, but the emperor would not relent.

sentences.zh: 無何，大理寺副曹荃發應恩賕請事，詞連至發。

translations.literal: Before long, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Cao Quan exposed Ying'en's bribery, with language implicating Zhifa.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Vice Minister Cao Quan of the Court of Judicial Review exposed Ying'en's bribery, implicating Zhifa.

sentences.zh: 至發憤，連疏請勘。

translations.literal: Zhifa in anger repeatedly memorialized requesting investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifa angrily submitted repeated memorials demanding investigation.

sentences.zh: 帝雖優旨褒答，卒下應恩獄。

translations.literal: Although the emperor answered with gracious edicts of praise, he ultimately sent Ying'en to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor replied with gracious edicts, he ultimately imprisoned Ying'en.

sentences.zh: 至發乃具疏，自謂當去者三，而未嘗引疾，忽得旨回籍調理，時人傳笑，以為遵旨患病雲。

translations.literal: Zhifa then fully memorialized, saying there were three reasons he ought to leave, yet he had never cited illness; suddenly he received an order to return home for recuperation—people laughed, saying he was 'obeying the edict by falling ill.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhifa then memorialized giving three reasons he should leave, though he had never cited illness; suddenly he was ordered home to recuperate—people mocked him for 'obeying the edict by falling ill.'

sentences.zh: 至發頗清強。

translations.literal: Zhifa was rather upright and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifa was a forceful, upright man.

sentences.zh: 起自外吏，諸翰林多不服，又始終惡異己，不能虛公延攬。

translations.literal: Rising from outside the Hanlin ranks, many Hanlin scholars looked down on him; he always hated those unlike himself and could not broadly recruit talent with impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: An outsider among the Hanlin, he was resented by many scholars and never welcomed rivals, failing to recruit talent impartially.

sentences.zh: 帝亦惡其泄漏機密，聽之去。

translations.literal: The emperor also disliked his leaking state secrets and let him go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also disliked his leaking secrets and allowed him to leave.

sentences.zh: 且不遣行人護行，但令乘傳，賜道里費六十金、彩幣二表裏，視首輔去國彜典，僅得半焉。

translations.literal: Moreover no imperial messenger was sent to escort him; he was only told to take relay horses, with sixty taels of traveling money and two rolls of silk brocade—only half the ritual due a departing chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: No imperial messenger escorted him; he was given relay horses, sixty taels, and two rolls of brocade—only half what a departing chief minister normally received.

sentences.zh: 既歸，捐貲改建淄城，賜敕優獎。

translations.literal: After returning home he donated funds to rebuild Zichuan city and received an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he donated funds to rebuild Zichuan and received an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 俄以徽號禮成，遣官存問。

translations.literal: Before long, when the posthumous title rites were completed, officials were sent to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after the posthumous-title rites were completed, officials were sent to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 十四年夏，帝思用舊臣，特敕召周延儒、賀逢聖及至發，獨至發四疏辭。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year the emperor thought to use old ministers and specially ordered the recall of Zhou Yanru, He Fengsheng, and Zhifa; Zhifa alone declined four times.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourteenth year the emperor recalled Zhou Yanru, He Fengsheng, and Zhifa; only Zhifa declined four times.

sentences.zh: 明年七月病歿。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the following year he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the following year he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 先屢加太子太傅、禮部尚書、文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: He had repeatedly been given the titles Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth.
translations.idiomatic: He had repeatedly been made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth.

sentences.zh: 及卒，贈少保，祭葬，蔭子如制。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously made Junior Guardian, with state sacrifices and hereditary privilege for his son as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Junior Guardian, with state sacrifices and hereditary privilege for his son as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 代至發為首輔者，孔貞運。

translations.literal: The one who replaced Zhifa as chief minister was Kong Zhenyun.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhenyun succeeded Zhifa as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 代貞運者，劉宇亮。

translations.literal: The one who replaced Zhenyun was Liu Yuliang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuliang succeeded Zhenyun.

sentences.zh: 貞運，句容人，至聖十三代孫也。

translations.literal: Zhenyun was a native of Jurong and a thirteenth-generation descendant of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyun came from Jurong and was a thirteenth-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十七年以殿試第二人授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Wanli he placed second in the palace examination and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year of Wanli he placed second in the palace examination and was appointed Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，充經筵展書官，纂修《兩朝實錄》。

translations.literal: During Tianqi he served as lecturer at the classics mat and helped compile the Veritable Records of the Two Reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he lectured at the classics mat and helped compile the Veritable Records of the Two Reigns.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝嗣位，貞運進講《皇明寶訓》，稱述祖宗勤政講學事，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded, Zhenyun lectured on the Imperial Instructions of the Ming and praised the diligence and study of the founding ancestors; the emperor commended and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: At Chongzhen's accession Zhenyun lectured on the Imperial Instructions, praising the founders' diligence and study; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，擢國子監祭酒，尋進少詹，仍管監事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was promoted to Director of the Imperial Academy, then Junior Mentor while still overseeing the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he became Director of the Imperial Academy, then Junior Mentor while retaining charge of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，帝臨雍，貞運進講《書經》。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the emperor visited the Academy; Zhenyun lectured on the Book of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year the emperor visited the Academy and Zhenyun lectured on the Book of Documents.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀時，祭酒孔穎達講《孝經》，有釋奠頌。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era of Tang, Director Kong Yingda lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and there was a libation hymn.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang's Zhenguan era Director Kong Yingda lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety with a libation hymn.

sentences.zh: 孔氏子孫以國師進講，至貞運乃再見。

translations.literal: A descendant of the Kong clan lecturing as state teacher was seen again only with Zhenyun.
translations.idiomatic: A Kong descendant lecturing as state teacher was not seen again until Zhenyun.

sentences.zh: 帝以聖裔故，從優賜一品服。

translations.literal: Because he was of sage descent, the emperor granted him first-rank robes as a special favor.
translations.idiomatic: As a descendant of the sage, the emperor granted him first-rank robes as a special honor.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，畿輔被兵，條上御敵城守應援數策。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter the capital region suffered military incursion; he submitted several plans for defense, garrison, and relief.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the capital region was invaded; he submitted plans for defense, garrison duty, and relief.

sentences.zh: 尋以艱歸。

translations.literal: Before long he returned home on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned home to mourn a parent.

sentences.zh: 六年服闋，起南京禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended in the sixth year he was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended in the sixth year he was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 越二年，遷吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Two years later he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was made Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年六月，與賀逢聖、黃士俊並入內閣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year he entered the Grand Secretariat together with He Fengsheng and Huang Shijun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year he entered the Grand Secretariat with He Fengsheng and Huang Shijun.

sentences.zh: 時體仁當國，欲重治復社，值其在告，貞運從寬結之。

translations.literal: At that time Tiren held power and wished to punish the Fushe society severely; while he was on leave Zhenyun settled the matter leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren then ruled and wished to punish the Fushe society harshly; during his leave Zhenyun settled the case leniently.

sentences.zh: 體仁怒語人曰：「句容亦聽人提索矣。」

translations.literal: Tiren said angrily to others: "Even Jurong lets people pull him around by the nose now."
translations.idiomatic: Tiren said angrily: "Even Jurong lets people lead him by the nose now."

sentences.zh: 自是不敢有所建白。

translations.literal: From then on Zhenyun did not dare offer proposals.
translations.idiomatic: After that Zhenyun dared not offer proposals.

sentences.zh: 及至發去位，貞運代之，乃揭救鄭三俊、錢謙益，俱從寬擬。

translations.literal: When Zhifa left office Zhenyun replaced him and then submitted a joint memorial to save Zheng Sanjun and Qian Qianyi, both treated leniently.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhifa left, Zhenyun succeeded him and submitted a joint memorial saving Zheng Sanjun and Qian Qianyi, both treated leniently.

sentences.zh: 帝親定考選諸臣，下輔臣再閱，貞運及薛國觀有所更。

translations.literal: The emperor personally fixed the examination selections; the chief ministers were to review them again, and Zhenyun and Xue Guoguan made changes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally chose examination candidates for the ministers to review; Zhenyun and Xue Guoguan altered his list.

sentences.zh: 迨命下，閣擬悉不從，而帝以所擇十八卷下部議行。

translations.literal: When the order was issued the secretariat's nominations were all rejected, and the emperor sent his own eighteen scrolls down for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When the order came down the secretariat's list was rejected and the emperor's eighteen chosen scrolls were sent for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 適新御史郭景昌等謁貞運於朝房，貞運言所下諸卷，說多難行。

translations.literal: The new censor Guo Jingchang and others called on Zhenyun in the court lodging; Zhenyun said the issued scrolls were mostly hard to implement.
translations.idiomatic: New censor Guo Jingchang called on Zhenyun in the court lodging; Zhenyun said the issued scrolls were mostly impractical.

sentences.zh: 景昌與辯，退即上疏劾之。

translations.literal: Jingchang argued with him and, on retiring, immediately memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchang argued with him and, on leaving, immediately impeached him.

sentences.zh: 帝雖奪景昌俸，貞運卒引歸。

translations.literal: Although the emperor stripped Jingchang of salary, Zhenyun ultimately resigned and went home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fined Jingchang's salary, but Zhenyun ultimately resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 十七年五月，莊烈帝哀詔至，貞運哭臨，慟絕不能起。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year, when the Chongzhen Emperor's mourning edict arrived, Zhenyun wept at the announcement and was overcome with grief and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year, when the Chongzhen Emperor's mourning edict arrived, Zhenyun wept at the proclamation and collapsed in grief.

sentences.zh: 舁歸，得疾遽卒。

translations.literal: Carried home, he fell suddenly ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Carried home, he fell suddenly ill and died.

sentences.zh: 黃士俊，順德人。

translations.literal: Huang Shijun was a native of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shijun was from Shunde.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十五年殿試第一。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Wanli he ranked first in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 35 he took first place in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 授修撰，歷官禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler and rose to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Compiler, he rose to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 崇禎九年入閣，累加少傅，予告歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chongzhen he entered the Grand Secretariat, was repeatedly promoted to Junior Mentor, and was granted leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 9 he entered the secretariat, was made Junior Mentor, and took leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 父母俱在堂，錦衣侍養，人以為榮。

translations.literal: With both parents still alive in the hall, he attended them in brocade robes, and people regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Both parents still alive, he attended them in official brocade—a thing others regarded as glory.

sentences.zh: 唐王以原官召，未赴。

translations.literal: The Prince of Tang summoned him to his former post, but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tang recalled him to his former post; he did not go.

sentences.zh: 後相永明王，耄不能決事，數為臺省論列。

translations.literal: Later he served as counselor to the Prince of Yongming; in old age he could not decide affairs and was repeatedly criticized by censorial and secretariat officials.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served the Prince of Yongming; too aged to decide affairs, he was repeatedly attacked by censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 辭歸而卒。

translations.literal: He resigned and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned, returned home, and died.

sentences.zh: 劉宇亮

translations.literal: Liu Yuliang
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuliang

sentences.zh: 劉宇亮，綿竹人。

translations.literal: Liu Yuliang was a native of Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuliang was from Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十七年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the forty-seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Wanli 47.

sentences.zh: 屢遷吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年八月，擢禮部尚書，與傅冠、薛國觀同入閣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the tenth year of Chongzhen he was promoted to Minister of Rites and entered the Grand Secretariat together with Fu Guan and Xue Guoguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chongzhen 10 he was made Minister of Rites and entered the secretariat with Fu Guan and Xue Guoguan.

sentences.zh: 宇亮短小精悍，善擊劍。

translations.literal: Yuliang was short, sharp, and vigorous, and skilled at swordplay.
translations.idiomatic: Short and fierce, Yuliang was skilled at swordplay.

sentences.zh: 居翰林，常與家僮角逐為樂。

translations.literal: While in the Hanlin, he often competed for amusement with his household servants.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hanlin he often raced his servants for sport.

sentences.zh: 性不嗜書，館中纂修、直講、典試諸事，皆不得與。

translations.literal: By nature he did not love books; in the academy he was excluded from compilation, lecturing, and examination duties.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for books and was barred from compilation, lecturing, and examination duties.

sentences.zh: 座主錢士升為之援，又力排同鄉王應熊，張己聲譽，竟獲大用。

translations.literal: His patron Qian Shisheng backed him; he also worked hard to exclude his fellow townsman Wang Yingxiong, inflated his own reputation, and ultimately won great appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Patron Qian Shisheng backed him; he sidelined fellow townsman Wang Yingxiong, burnished his own name, and won high office.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，貞運罷歸，遂代為首輔。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year Zhenyun was dismissed and went home, and Yuliang then replaced him as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The next sixth month Zhenyun resigned; Yuliang succeeded him as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 其冬，都城戒嚴，命閱視三大營及勇衛營軍士，兩日而畢。

translations.literal: That winter the capital was placed under martial law; he was ordered to inspect the troops of the Three Great Camps and the Brave Guard Camp, finishing in two days.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the capital went on alert; ordered to inspect the Three Great Camps and Brave Guard Camp, he finished in two days.

sentences.zh: 又閱視內城九門，外城七門，皆茍且卒事。

translations.literal: He also inspected the nine gates of the inner city and seven gates of the outer city, finishing each perfunctorily.
translations.idiomatic: He also inspected the inner city's nine gates and outer city's seven—all perfunctorily dispatched.

sentences.zh: 時大清兵深入，帝憂甚，宇亮自請督察軍情。

translations.literal: At that time Great Qing forces had penetrated deep; the emperor was greatly worried, and Yuliang volunteered to inspect military conditions.
translations.idiomatic: With Qing forces deep inside the realm, the emperor was deeply worried; Yuliang volunteered to inspect the armies.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，即革總督盧象升任，命宇亮往代。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and immediately removed supreme commander Lu Xiangsheng from office, ordering Yuliang to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased, the emperor removed supreme commander Lu Xiangsheng and ordered Yuliang to replace him.

sentences.zh: 字亮請督察，而帝忽改為總督，大懼，與國觀及楊嗣昌謀，且具疏自言。

translations.literal: Yuliang had asked to inspect, but the emperor suddenly changed it to supreme commander—a post he greatly feared; he consulted Guoguan and Yang Sichang and submitted a memorial explaining himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang had asked to inspect, but the emperor suddenly made him supreme commander; terrified, he conspired with Guoguan and Yang Sichang and memorialized in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 乃留象升，而宇亮仍往督察，各鎮勤王兵皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Xiangsheng was kept in office, while Yuliang still went out as inspector; all troops from the provinces rushing to aid the throne were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangsheng was kept on; Yuliang still went out as inspector, with all provincial relief armies under his command.

sentences.zh: 甫抵保定，聞象升戰歿，過安平，偵者報大清兵將至，相顧無人色，急趨晉州避之，知州陳弘緒閉門不納，士民亦歃血誓不延一兵。

translations.literal: Just after reaching Baoding he heard Xiangsheng had died in battle; passing Anping, scouts reported Great Qing forces were coming—they looked at one another, pale as death, and hurried toward Jizhou to flee; Prefect Chen Hongxu closed the gates and would not admit them, and gentry and commoners likewise swore by blood not to let in a single soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Baoding, he learned Xiangsheng had fallen; near Anping scouts reported Qing forces approaching—they went white with fear and fled toward Jizhou; Prefect Chen Hongxu shut the gates, and townsfolk swore by blood to admit not one soldier.

sentences.zh: 宇亮大怒，傳令箭：亟納師，否則軍法從事。

translations.literal: Yuliang flew into a rage and sent a command arrow: admit the army at once or face military law.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang raged and sent a command arrow: admit the army at once or face military justice.

sentences.zh: 弘緒亦傳語曰：「督師之來以禦敵也，今敵且至，奈何避之？

translations.literal: Hongxu sent back word as well: "The supervising commander came to resist the enemy; now the enemy is about to arrive—why flee?
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu replied: "The supervising commander came to fight the enemy; the enemy is near—why flee?

sentences.zh: 芻糧不繼，責有司，欲入城，不敢聞命。」

translations.literal: Fodder and grain cannot be supplied; blame the responsible officials. You wish to enter the city—I dare not obey such an order."
translations.idiomatic: Fodder runs short—blame the officials. You seek entry—I dare not obey."

sentences.zh: 宇亮乃馳疏劾之，有旨逮治。

translations.literal: Yuliang then sent a hasty memorial impeaching him, and an edict ordered him seized for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang hastily impeached him; an edict ordered his arrest.

sentences.zh: 州民詣闕訟冤，願以身代者千計，弘緒得鐫級調用。

translations.literal: People of the prefecture went to the palace to plead injustice; over a thousand offered to take his place, and Hongxu was merely reduced one rank and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Prefecture folk went to court pleading injustice; a thousand offered to die in his place; Hongxu was reduced one rank and transferred.

sentences.zh: 帝自是疑宇亮不任事，徒擾民矣。

translations.literal: From then on the emperor doubted that Yuliang was equal to the task and only harassed the people.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor doubted Yuliang's competence and thought he only harassed the people.

sentences.zh: 明年正月至天津。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he reached Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: The next first month he reached Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 憤諸將退避，疏論之，因及總兵劉光祚逗遛狀。

translations.literal: Angered at the generals' retreat, he memorialized criticizing them and also cited Regional Commander Liu Guangzuo's delays.
translations.idiomatic: Angered at the generals' retreats, he memorialized against them and cited Regional Commander Liu Guangzuo's stalling.

sentences.zh: 國觀方冀為首輔，與嗣昌謀傾宇亮，遽擬旨軍前斬光祚。

translations.literal: Guoguan was hoping to become chief minister; conspiring with Sichang to bring down Yuliang, he quickly drafted an edict to execute Guangzuo before the army.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan, hoping for chief minister, conspired with Sichang to ruin Yuliang and swiftly drafted an edict to behead Guangzuo at the front.

sentences.zh: 比旨下，光祚適有武清之捷，宇亮乃系光祚於獄，而具疏乞宥，繼上武清捷音。

translations.literal: When the edict arrived Guangzuo had just won a victory at Wuqing; Yuliang then imprisoned Guangzuo but memorialized asking pardon, then submitted news of the Wuqing victory.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived Guangzuo had just won at Wuqing; Yuliang imprisoned him but memorialized for pardon, then reported the Wuqing victory.

sentences.zh: 國觀乃擬嚴旨，責以前後矛盾，下九卿科道議。

translations.literal: Guoguan then drafted a harsh edict faulting the contradiction and sent the matter down to the Nine Ministers and censorate for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan drafted a harsh edict citing Yuliang's contradiction and sent the case to the Nine Ministers and censorate.

sentences.zh: 僉謂宇亮玩弄國憲，大不敬。

translations.literal: All agreed Yuliang had trifled with state law—a grave lack of respect.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed Yuliang had mocked state law—a grave offense.

sentences.zh: 宇亮疏辯，部議落職閑住，給事中陳啟新、沈迅復重劾之，改擬削籍。

translations.literal: Yuliang memorialized in defense; the ministry recommended dismissal and idle residence; supervising secretaries Chen Qixin and Shen Xun impeached him again, changing the recommendation to stripping from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang defended himself; the ministry recommended dismissal; supervising secretaries Chen Qixin and Shen Xun impeached him again, changing the penalty to strippage from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 帝令戴罪圖功，事平再議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to bear guilt while striving for merit and to be reconsidered when affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to redeem himself through merit and be judged again when peace returned.

sentences.zh: 宇亮竟以此去位，而國觀代為首輔矣。

translations.literal: Yuliang ultimately left office over this, and Guoguan replaced him as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliang ultimately fell over this, and Guoguan became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 已而定失事者五案，宇亮終免議。

translations.literal: Later five cases of dereliction were fixed, and Yuliang was ultimately spared deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Later five dereliction cases were settled, and Yuliang was spared further judgment.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long while he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died at home.

sentences.zh: 薛國觀

translations.literal: Xue Guoguan
translations.idiomatic: Xue Guoguan

sentences.zh: 薛國觀，韓城人。

translations.literal: Xue Guoguan was a native of Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Guoguan was from Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十七年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the forty-seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Wanli 47.

sentences.zh: 授萊州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed pushing official of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed subprefectural judge in Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，擢戶部給事中，數有建白。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Ministry of Revenue and often offered proposals.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 4 he became a revenue supervising secretary and often offered proposals.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢擅權，朝士爭擊東林。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian monopolized power, and court officials competed to attack the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: With Wei Zhongxian in power, court officials competed to attack the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 國觀所劾御史遊士任、操江都御史熊明遇、保定巡撫張鳳翔、兵部侍郎蕭近高、刑部尚書喬允升，皆東林也。

translations.literal: The censor You Shiren, Grand Coordinator of River Defense Xiong Mingyu, Grand Coordinator of Baoding Zhang Fengxiang, Vice Minister of War Xiao Jin'gao, and Minister of Justice Qiao Yunsheng whom Guoguan impeached were all Donglin men.
translations.idiomatic: Censor You Shiren, River Defense Coordinator Xiong Mingyu, Baoding Coordinator Zhang Fengxiang, Vice Minister of War Xiao Jin'gao, and Minister of Justice Qiao Yunsheng—all Donglin men—were impeached by Guoguan.

sentences.zh: 尋遷兵科右給事中，於疆事亦多所論奏。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and also memorialized much on frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon made right supervising secretary of military affairs, he memorialized often on frontier matters.

sentences.zh: 忠賢遣內臣出鎮，偕同官疏爭。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian sent eunuchs to command garrisons, Guoguan joined colleagues in memorializing against it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian posted eunuchs to frontier commands, Guoguan joined colleagues in protesting.

sentences.zh: 七年，再遷刑科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he rose to chief supervising secretary of punishments.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，忠賢遺黨有欲用王化貞，寬高，出胡嘉棟者，國觀力持不可。

translations.literal: When Chongzhen took the throne, remnants of Zhongxian's faction wished to restore Wang Huazhen, show leniency to Gao Yingxian, and release Hu Jiadong; Guoguan strongly held this impossible.
translations.idiomatic: At Chongzhen's accession, Zhongxian's remnants sought to restore Wang Huazhen, leniency for Gao Yingxian, and Hu Jiadong's release; Guoguan forcefully opposed it.

sentences.zh: 奉命祭北鎮醫無閭，還言關內外營伍虛耗、將吏侵克之弊，因薦大將滿桂才。

translations.literal: Ordered to sacrifice at the northern shrine of Yiwu Lü, on returning he spoke of the waste of inner and outer garrison forces and the abuses of officers embezzling supplies, and recommended the great general Man Gui's talent.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to sacrifice at the northern shrine of Yiwu Lü, he returned reporting wasted garrisons and officers' embezzlement, recommending the great general Man Gui.

sentences.zh: 帝褒以忠讜，令指將吏侵克者名，列上副將王應暉等六人，詔俱屬之吏。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his loyal candor and ordered him to name officers guilty of embezzlement; he listed Deputy General Wang Yinghui and five others, and an edict turned them all over to the ministry for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his candor and ordered names of embezzling officers; he listed Deputy General Wang Yinghui and five others, whom an edict turned over for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 陜西盜起，偕鄉人仕於朝者，請設防速剿，並追論故巡撫喬應甲納賄縱盜罪。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Shaanxi, together with fellow townsmen serving at court he requested rapid defense and suppression, and also pursued the former Grand Coordinator Qiao Yingjia's crimes of taking bribes and indulging bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi bandits rose, he and fellow Hancheng officials at court called for swift defense and renewed charges against former coordinator Qiao Yingjia for bribery and indulging bandits.

sentences.zh: 削應甲籍，籍其贓。

translations.literal: Yingjia was struck from the rolls and his illicit gains were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjia was struck from the rolls and his gains confiscated.

sentences.zh: 國觀先附忠賢，至是大治忠賢黨，為南京御史袁耀然所劾。

translations.literal: Guoguan had first attached himself to Zhongxian; now he vigorously prosecuted Zhongxian's faction and was impeached by Nanjing censor Yuan Yaoran.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhongxian's ally, Guoguan now prosecuted his faction and was impeached by Nanjing censor Yuan Yaoran.

sentences.zh: 國觀懼，且虞掛察典，思所以撓之，乃劾吏科都給事中沈惟炳、兵科給事中許譽卿，言：「兩人主盟東林，與瞿式耜掌握枚卜。

translations.literal: Guoguan was afraid and also feared being caught in the capital evaluation; thinking how to obstruct it, he impeached Chief Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Personnel Shen Weibing and Supervising Secretary of Military Affairs Xu Yuqing, saying: "The two lead the Donglin alliance and, with Qu Shisi, control official selection.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid and fearing entanglement in the capital evaluation, Guoguan impeached Shen Weibing and Xu Yuqing, saying: "Both lead the Donglin and, with Qu Shisi, control official selection.

sentences.zh: 文華召對，陛下惡章允儒妄言，嚴旨處分。

translations.literal: At Wenhua Hall audiences, Your Majesty hated Zhang Yunru's reckless speech and issued harsh edicts of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenhua audiences the Emperor hated Zhang Yunru's reckless talk and issued harsh punishment.

sentences.zh: 譽卿乃持一疏授惟炳，使同官劉斯珣邀臣列名，臣拒不應，遂使耀然劾臣。

translations.literal: Yuqing then handed a memorial to Weibing and had colleague Liu Sixun invite me to sign; I refused, so he had Yaoran impeach me.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing handed a memorial to Weibing and had Liu Sixun ask me to sign; I refused, so he set Yaoran on me.

sentences.zh: 臣自立有品，不入東林，遂罹其害。

translations.literal: I have always stood on my own principle and did not join the Donglin—thus I suffered their harm.
translations.idiomatic: I have always stood apart and never joined the Donglin—so they struck at me.

sentences.zh: 今朝局惟論東林異同向背，借崔、魏為題，報仇傾陷。

translations.literal: Today's court concerns itself only with whether one is for or against the Donglin, using Cui and Wei as pretexts for revenge and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Today's court cares only whether one is for or against the Donglin, using Cui and Wei as pretexts for revenge.

sentences.zh: 今又把持京察，而式耜以被斥之人，久居郭外，遙制察典，舉朝無敢言。」

translations.literal: Now they monopolize the capital evaluation, while Shisi—a dismissed man long dwelling outside the walls—controls the evaluation from afar, and no one in court dares speak."
translations.idiomatic: Now they control the capital evaluation while Shisi, long banished outside the walls, steers it from afar—and none in court dare speak."

sentences.zh: 末詆耀然賄劉鴻訓得御史。

translations.literal: At the end he slandered Yaoran for bribing Liu Hongxun to obtain the censor's post.
translations.idiomatic: He ended by accusing Yaoran of bribing Liu Hongxun for the censorate.

sentences.zh: 帝雖以撓察典責之，國觀卒免察。

translations.literal: Although the emperor rebuked him for obstructing the evaluation, Guoguan ultimately escaped it.
translations.idiomatic: Though rebuked for obstructing the evaluation, Guoguan ultimately escaped it.

sentences.zh: 然清議不容，旋以終養去。

translations.literal: Yet public opinion would not tolerate him, and he soon left on grounds of final mourning for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion would not bear him, and he soon retired on grounds of final parental mourning.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，用御史陳其猷薦，起兵科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year, on censor Chen Qiyou's recommendation, he was made Chief Supervising Secretary of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year's autumn, on censor Chen Qiyou's recommendation, he became chief supervising secretary of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，服闋，起禮科都給事中，遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when mourning ended he was recalled as Chief Supervising Secretary of Rites and promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was recalled as chief rites supervising secretary and promoted Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢左僉都御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，拜禮部左侍郎兼東閣大學士，入參機務。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Lodge, entering to deliberate on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next eighth month he was made Vice Minister of Rites and Eastern Lodge Grand Secretary, joining state deliberations.

sentences.zh: 國觀為人陰鷙谿刻，不學少文。

translations.literal: Guoguan was secretive, harsh, and narrow-minded, lacking learning and literary polish.
translations.idiomatic: Secretive, harsh, and narrow, Guoguan lacked learning and polish.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁因其素仇東林，密薦於帝，遂超擢大用之。

translations.literal: Wen Tiren, because Guoguan had long hated the Donglin, secretly recommended him to the emperor, and he was abruptly promoted to great use.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren, knowing Guoguan's hatred of the Donglin, secretly recommended him and he was abruptly raised to high power.

sentences.zh: 十一年六月，進禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eleventh year he was advanced to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eleventh year he became Minister of Rites.
