sentences.zh: 其冬，首輔劉宇亮出督師，國觀與楊嗣昌比，構罷宇亮。

translations.literal: That winter chief minister Liu Yuliang went out as supervising commander; Guoguan aligned with Yang Sichang and engineered Yuliang's dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: That winter chief minister Yuliang went out to command; Guoguan joined Yang Sichang and engineered his fall.

sentences.zh: 明年二月代其位。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he replaced Yuliang's place.
translations.idiomatic: The next second month he took Yuliang's place.

sentences.zh: 敘剿寇功，加太子太保、戶部尚書，進文淵閣；

translations.literal: Recording merit in suppressing bandits, he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Revenue and advanced to the Hall of Literary Depth;
translations.idiomatic: For bandit-suppression merit he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Revenue and entered the Hall of Literary Depth;

sentences.zh: 敘城守功，加少保、吏部尚書，進武英殿。

translations.literal: Recording merit in defending the city, he was given Junior Guardian and Minister of Personnel and advanced to the Hall of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: For defending the capital he was made Junior Guardian and Minister of Personnel and entered the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 先為首輔者，體仁最當帝意，居位久。

translations.literal: Of those who had been chief minister before, Tiren best matched the emperor's will and held office longest.
translations.idiomatic: Of earlier chief ministers, Tiren best pleased the emperor and lasted longest.

sentences.zh: 及張至發、孔貞運、劉宇亮繼之，皆非帝意所屬，故旋罷去。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhifa, Kong Zhenyun, and Liu Yuliang followed, none were the emperor's choice, and so were soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhifa, Kong Zhenyun, and Liu Yuliang who followed were none the emperor's men and were soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 國觀得誌，一踵體仁所為，導帝以深刻，而才智彌不及，操守亦弗如。

translations.literal: Guoguan having gotten his wish, wholly followed what Tiren had done, guiding the emperor toward harsh severity, yet his talent and wisdom fell even shorter and his integrity was inferior.
translations.idiomatic: In power, Guoguan wholly copied Tiren, steering the emperor toward harshness—yet fell even shorter in talent and integrity.

sentences.zh: 帝初頗信響之，久而覺其奸，遂及於禍。

translations.literal: At first the emperor quite trusted and responded to him, but in time perceived his treachery and disaster followed.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor trusted him; in time he saw the treachery—and ruin followed.

sentences.zh: 始帝燕見國觀，語及朝士貪婪。

translations.literal: When the emperor first met Guoguan informally, they spoke of court officials' greed.
translations.idiomatic: At an informal audience the emperor spoke with Guoguan of official greed.

sentences.zh: 國觀對曰：「使廠衛得人，安敢如是。」

translations.literal: Guoguan replied: "If the Brocade Guard and prison service had the right men, how would they dare act so."
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan replied: "If the secret police had able men, who would dare act so."

sentences.zh: 東廠太監王德化在側，汗流沾背，於是專察其陰事。

translations.literal: Eastern Depot eunuch Wang Dehua stood beside them, sweat soaking his back; from then on he devoted himself to investigating Guoguan's secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Depot director Wang Dehua stood by, sweat drenching his back—and from then on devoted himself to Guoguan's secrets.

sentences.zh: 國觀任中書王陛彥，而惡中書周國興、楊余洪，以漏詔旨、招權利劾之，並下詔獄。

translations.literal: Guoguan trusted Secretariat Drafter Wang Biyan but hated drafters Zhou Guoxing and Yang Yuhong, impeaching them for leaking edicts and seeking power and profit, and both were sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan favored drafter Wang Biyan but hated Zhou Guoxing and Yang Yuhong, impeaching them for leaking edicts and profiteering; both went to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 兩人老矣，斃廷杖下，其家人密緝國觀通賄事，報東廠。

translations.literal: Both were old and died under court beating; their families secretly gathered evidence of Guoguan's bribery connections and reported to the Eastern Depot.
translations.idiomatic: Both old men died under the beating; their families secretly gathered evidence of Guoguan's bribery and reported to the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 而國觀前匿史褷所寄銀，周、楊兩家又誘褷蒼頭首告。

translations.literal: Moreover Guoguan had earlier hidden silver entrusted by Shi Kun; the Zhou and Yang families also induced Shi Kun's servant to confess first.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan had hidden silver entrusted by Shi Kun; the Zhou and Yang families also turned Shi Kun's servant informant.

sentences.zh: 由是諸事悉上聞，帝意漸移。

translations.literal: Thus all matters reached the emperor's ears and his attitude gradually shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Everything reached the emperor, and his favor gradually turned.

sentences.zh: 史褷者，清苑人。

translations.literal: Shi Kun was a native of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kun was from Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 為御史無行，善結納中官，為王永光死黨。

translations.literal: As a censor he was without conduct, skilled at cultivating eunuchs, and a sworn follower of Wang Yongguang.
translations.idiomatic: A censor of no character, he cultivated eunuchs and was Wang Yongguang's sworn follower.

sentences.zh: 巡按淮、揚，括庫中贓罰銀十余萬入己橐。

translations.literal: Touring as inspector of Huai and Yang, he seized more than a hundred thousand taels of fine and penalty silver from the treasury for his own purse.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting Huai and Yang, he pocketed over 100,000 taels of fines from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 攝巡鹽，又掩取前官張錫命貯庫銀二十余萬。

translations.literal: Acting salt inspector, he also seized more than two hundred thousand taels stored by his predecessor Zhang Ximing.
translations.idiomatic: Acting salt inspector, he seized over 200,000 taels his predecessor Zhang Ximing had stored.

sentences.zh: 及以少卿家居，檢討楊士聰劾吏部尚書田唯嘉納周汝弼金八千推延綏巡撫，褷居間，並發褷盜鹽課事。

translations.literal: When he was at home as a vice minister, reviewer Yang Shicong impeached Minister of Personnel Tian Weijia for accepting eight thousand taels from Zhou Rubi to push him as Grand Coordinator of Yansui; Shi Kun had acted as go-between, and Shicong also exposed Shi Kun's theft of salt revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At home as a vice minister, reviewer Yang Shicong impeached Minister Tian Weijia for taking eight thousand taels from Zhou Rubi to secure the Yansui coordinator post—with Shi Kun as broker—and exposed Shi Kun's salt revenue theft.

sentences.zh: 褷得旨自陳，遂訐士聰，而鹽課則請敕淮、揚監督中官楊顯名核奏。

translations.literal: Shi Kun received an edict to explain himself, then accused Shicong in turn, and regarding salt revenue requested an edict for the Huai-Yang supervising eunuch Yang Xianming to verify and report.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kun was ordered to explain himself and counter-attacked Shicong; on salt revenue he asked the Huai-Yang supervising eunuch Yang Xianming to investigate.

sentences.zh: 俄而錫命子沆訐褷，給事中劉焜芳復劾褷侵盜有據。

translations.literal: Before long Zhang Ximing's son Hang accused Shi Kun, and supervising secretary Liu Kunfang again impeached him with evidence of embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Ximing's son Hang accused Shi Kun, and supervising secretary Liu Kunfang impeached him again with proof of theft.

sentences.zh: 又嘗勒富人於承祖萬金，事發，則遣家人賫重貲謀於黠吏，圖改舊籍。

translations.literal: He had also extorted ten thousand taels of gold from the wealthy man Yu Chengzu; when the matter broke, he sent family members bearing heavy bribes to clever clerks to alter the old records.
translations.idiomatic: He had extorted ten thousand taels from the magnate Yu Chengzu; when exposed, he sent family with heavy bribes to clever clerks to falsify the records.

sentences.zh: 帝乃怒，褫褷職，褷急攜數萬金入都，主國觀邸。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, stripped Shi Kun of office, and Shi Kun hurriedly carried tens of thousands of taels of gold to the capital and lodged at Guoguan's residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped him of office; Shi Kun hurried to the capital with tens of thousands of taels and lodged at Guoguan's house.

sentences.zh: 謀既定，出疏攻焜芳及其弟炳芳、煒芳。

translations.literal: Once the plot was set, he submitted a memorial attacking Kunfang and his brothers Bingfang and Weifang.
translations.idiomatic: Plot in place, he memorialized against Kunfang and his brothers Bingfang and Weifang.

sentences.zh: 閣臣多徇褷，擬嚴旨，帝不聽，止奪焜芳官候訊。

translations.literal: Most grand secretaries sided with Shi Kun and drafted a harsh edict, but the emperor would not listen and only stripped Kunfang of office pending inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Most grand secretaries sided with Shi Kun and drafted a harsh edict; the emperor refused and only stripped Kunfang pending inquiry.

sentences.zh: 及顯名核疏上，力為褷解，而不能諱者六萬金；

translations.literal: When Xianming's verified memorial reached the throne, he vigorously defended Shi Kun, but what could not be concealed was sixty thousand taels in gold;
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xianming's verification memorial arrived, Guoguan fought hard to clear Shi Kun—yet sixty thousand taels in gold could not be hidden.

sentences.zh: 褷下獄。

translations.literal: Shi Kun was sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kun went to prison.

sentences.zh: 會有兵事，獄久不結，瘐死。

translations.literal: Just then military affairs broke out; the case long went unsettled, and he died in prison of neglect.
translations.idiomatic: War intervened; the case dragged on, and he wasted away and died in custody.

sentences.zh: 都人籍籍謂褷所攜貲盡為國觀有，家人證之，事大著。

translations.literal: Capital folk gossiped that all the wealth Shi Kun had brought was now Guoguan's; the family confirmed it, and the affair became glaringly public.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing whispered that Shi Kun's baggage had all ended up with Guoguan; kin bore witness, and the scandal broke wide open.

sentences.zh: 國觀猶力辨褷贓為黨人構陷，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Guoguan still strenuously argued that Shi Kun's guilt was a factional frame-up; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan still insisted Shi Kun had been framed by factional enemies; the emperor refused to hear it.

sentences.zh: 帝初憂國用不足，國觀請借助，言：「在外群僚，臣等任之；

translations.literal: At first the emperor worried that state revenue was insufficient; Guoguan requested forced loans, saying: "For outer officials, your ministers can answer;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first fretted over empty coffers; Guoguan proposed forced "loans," saying: "Out in the provinces, we ministers can handle the rest;

sentences.zh: 在內戚畹，非獨斷不可。」

translations.literal: For inner consort kin, nothing but Your Majesty's sole decision will do."
translations.idiomatic: but among the imperial in-laws at court, only Your Majesty can decide."

sentences.zh: 因以武清侯李國瑞為言。

translations.literal: He took as his example Martial Tranquility Marquis Li Guorui.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to Martial Tranquility Marquis Li Guorui.

sentences.zh: 國瑞者，孝定太后兄孫，帝曾祖母家也。

translations.literal: Guorui was a grandson of Empress Dowager Xiaoding's elder brother—the house of the emperor's great-grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Guorui was a grandson on Empress Dowager Xiaoding's side—the emperor's maternal great-grandmother's kin.

sentences.zh: 國瑞薄庶兄國臣，國臣憤，詭言「父貲四十萬，臣當得其半，今請助國為軍貲」。

translations.literal: Guorui slighted his elder half-brother Guochen; Guochen, enraged, falsely claimed: "Our father's estate was four hundred thousand taels; I should have half; I now ask to loan the state military funds."
translations.idiomatic: Guorui scorned his elder half-brother Guochen, who in anger fabricated a tale: "Father left four hundred thousand taels; half is mine—I offer it now to aid the army."

sentences.zh: 帝初未允，因國觀言，欲盡借所言四十萬者，不應則勒期嚴追。

translations.literal: At first the emperor did not agree, but because of Guoguan's words he wished to borrow the full four hundred thousand taels claimed; if Guorui refused, a strict deadline would be set for collection.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first refused, but swayed by Guoguan he meant to seize all of the claimed four hundred thousand—and if Guorui balked, pursue him on a hard deadline.

sentences.zh: 或教國瑞匿貲勿獻，拆毀居第，陳什器通衢鬻之，示無所有。

translations.literal: Some advised Guorui to hide his wealth and not submit, to tear down his mansion and sell household goods in the open street to show he owned nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors urged Guorui to conceal his fortune, demolish his house, and hawk his furnishings in the public way to prove poverty.

sentences.zh: 嘉定伯周奎與有連，代為請。

translations.literal: Duke of Jiading Zhou Kui was connected to him and pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Jiading Duke Zhou Kui, a relation, interceded for him.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪國瑞爵，國瑞悸死。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, stripped Guorui of his rank, and Guorui died of fright.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in fury took Guorui's title; Guorui died of terror.

sentences.zh: 有司追不已，戚畹皆自危。

translations.literal: The authorities kept pressing the collection without cease, and all consort kin felt themselves in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Officials kept dunning him, and every imperial relative trembled.

sentences.zh: 因皇五子病，交通宦官宮妾，倡言孝定太后已為九蓮菩薩，空中責帝薄外家，諸皇子盡當夭，降神於皇五子。

translations.literal: Because the fifth imperial son fell ill, they reached through palace eunuchs and concubines, spreading word that Empress Dowager Xiaoding had become the Nine-Lotus Bodhisattva, that a voice in the air rebuked the emperor for slighting his maternal kin, that all princes were doomed to die young, and that a spirit possessed the fifth prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the fifth prince sickened, eunuchs and palace women were enlisted to claim Xiaoding had become the Nine-Lotus Bodhisattva, that heaven rebuked the emperor for coldness toward his in-laws, that every prince would die young—and that a spirit had entered the fifth son.

sentences.zh: 俄皇子卒，帝大恐，急封國瑞七歲兒存善為侯，盡還所納金銀，而追恨國觀，待隙而發。

translations.literal: Before long the prince died; the emperor was greatly terrified, hastily enfeoffed Guorui's seven-year-old son Cunshan as marquis, fully returned the gold and silver taken, yet nursed hatred of Guoguan and waited for an opening to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the prince was dead; the emperor, terrified, made Guorui's seven-year-old Cunshan a marquis, returned every ingot seized—and still brooded on Guoguan, biding his time.

sentences.zh: 國觀素惡行人吳昌時。

translations.literal: Guoguan had long hated the courier Wu Changshi.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan had always despised courier Wu Changshi.

sentences.zh: 及考選，昌時虞國觀抑己，因其門人以求見。

translations.literal: When the examination selections came, Changshi feared Guoguan would hold him down and, through a disciple, sought an audience.
translations.idiomatic: At the selection examinations Changshi feared Guoguan would block him and used a protégé to gain access.

sentences.zh: 國觀偽與交歡，擬第一，當得吏科。

translations.literal: Guoguan feigned friendship, ranked him first, and said he should receive the post of supervising secretary in the Office of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan pretended warmth, put him first on the list, and promised him the personnel supervising secretaryship.

sentences.zh: 迨命下，乃得禮部主事。

translations.literal: When the appointment came down, he received only a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When orders issued, he got only a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 昌時大恨，以為賣己，與所善東廠理刑吳道正謀，發丁憂侍郎蔡奕琛行賄國觀事。

translations.literal: Changshi hated him deeply, believing he had sold him out, and with his ally Wu Daozheng, judge at the Eastern Depot, plotted to expose Vice Minister Cai Yichen, then in mourning, bribing Guoguan.
translations.idiomatic: Changshi, convinced he had been betrayed, conspired with Eastern Depot judge Wu Daozheng to expose mourning vice minister Cai Yichen's bribes to Guoguan.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，益疑。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, his suspicion deepened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard—and doubted all the more.

sentences.zh: 十三年六月，楊嗣昌出督師，有所陳奏。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year Yang Sichang went out as grand coordinator and submitted certain memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year thirteen Yang Sichang took field command and memorialized on several matters.

sentences.zh: 帝令擬諭，國觀乃擬旨以進。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a rescript drafted; Guoguan drafted the response and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a reply drafted; Guoguan wrote it and sent it in.

sentences.zh: 帝遂發怒，下五府九卿科道議奏。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon flew into rage and sent the matter down to the Five Offices, Nine Ministries, and the censorate for deliberation and memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor erupted and referred the matter to the Five Offices, Nine Ministries, and censorate for joint memorial.

sentences.zh: 掌都督府魏國公徐允禎、吏部尚書傅永淳等不測帝意，議頗輕，請令致仕或閑住。

translations.literal: Director of the Chief Military Commission, Wei State Duke Xu Yunzhen, Minister of Personnel Fu Yongchun, and others could not fathom the emperor's intent; their deliberation was rather lenient, asking that he be allowed to retire or be given idle appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yunzhen of Wei, chief of the military commission, Fu Yongchun of Personnel, and others misread the throne; their report was mild—retirement or idle post.

sentences.zh: 帝度科道必言之，獨給事中袁愷會議不署名，且疏論永淳徇私狀，而微詆國觀藐肆妒嫉。

translations.literal: The emperor expected the censorate would speak; only supervising secretary Yuan Kai at the conference refused to sign, and in a memorial detailed Yongchun's favoritism while subtly denouncing Guoguan's arrogance, jealousy, and insolence.
translations.idiomatic: He expected the censors to weigh in; only Yuan Kai withheld his signature at the conference, memorialized Yongchun's partiality, and quietly assailed Guoguan's arrogance and spite.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，抵疏於地曰：「成何糾疏！」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, dashed the memorial to the floor, and said: "What kind of impeachment is this!"
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor threw the paper down: "What sort of accusation is this!"

sentences.zh: 遂奪國觀職，放之歸，怒猶未已。

translations.literal: He thereupon stripped Guoguan of office and sent him home, yet his anger was still not spent.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped Guoguan and sent him home—but rage still burned.

sentences.zh: 國觀出都，重車累累，偵事者復以聞。

translations.literal: Guoguan left the capital with heavy wagons in long train; informants again reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan quit the capital under wagons piled high; spies reported it again.

sentences.zh: 而東廠所遣伺國觀邸者，值陛彥至，執之，得其招搖通賄狀。

translations.literal: Meanwhile an agent the Eastern Depot had sent to watch Guoguan's residence encountered Biyan arriving, seized him, and obtained evidence of swaggering bribery.
translations.idiomatic: An Eastern Depot watcher at Guoguan's house caught Biyan, seized him, and extracted confession of open bribery.

sentences.zh: 詞所連及，永淳、奕琛暨通政使李夢辰、刑部主事朱永佑等十一人。

translations.literal: His testimony implicated Yongchun, Yichen, Transmission Commissioner Li Mengchen, principal secretary of Punishments Zhu Yongyou, and eleven others in all.
translations.idiomatic: His words dragged in Yongchun, Yichen, Li Mengchen of the Transmission Office, Zhu Yongyou of Punishments, and eleven others.

sentences.zh: 命下陛彥詔獄窮治。

translations.literal: Orders went down to imprison Biyan in the imperial prison and investigate to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Biyan was ordered into the imperial prison for exhaustive inquiry.

sentences.zh: 頃之，愷再疏，盡發國觀納賄諸事，永淳、奕琛與焉。

translations.literal: Before long Kai memorialized again, fully exposing Guoguan's bribe-taking, Yongchun and Yichen among them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Kai memorialized again, laying bare Guoguan's graft—Yongchun and Yichen included.

sentences.zh: 國觀連疏力辨，詆愷受昌時指使，帝不納。

translations.literal: Guoguan memorialized repeatedly in fierce denial, accusing Kai of acting at Changshi's direction; the emperor would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan fought back in serial memorials, claiming Kai acted for Changshi; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 至十月，陛彥獄未成，帝以行賄有據，即命棄市，而遣使逮國觀。

translations.literal: By the tenth month Biyan's case was not yet finished, but the emperor, holding bribery proven, immediately ordered him executed in the marketplace and sent envoys to seize Guoguan.
translations.idiomatic: Come the tenth month the Biyan case remained open—yet with bribery deemed proven, the emperor ordered him beheaded and messengers sent for Guoguan.

sentences.zh: 國觀遷延久不赴，明年七月入都。

translations.literal: Guoguan delayed and long did not come; in the seventh month of the following year he entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan lingered abroad until the seventh month of the next year, then entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 令待命外邸，不以屬吏，國觀自謂必不死。

translations.literal: He was ordered to await orders at an outer lodge, not handed to the judicial officers; Guoguan told himself he would surely not die.
translations.idiomatic: He was told to wait at an outer lodge, not remanded to jail; Guoguan assured himself he would live.

sentences.zh: 八月初八日夕，監刑者至門，猶鼾睡。

translations.literal: On the evening of the eighth day of the eighth month the executioners reached his gate; he was still snoring in sleep.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth month's eighth evening the execution party came; he still slept.

sentences.zh: 及聞詔使皆緋衣，蹶然曰：「吾死矣！」

translations.literal: When he heard the edict-bearers all wore crimson robes, he started up and said: "I am dead!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the messengers wore crimson, he jolted awake: "I am finished!"

sentences.zh: 倉皇覓小帽不得，取蒼頭帽覆之。

translations.literal: In haste he sought a small cap and could not find one; he took a servant's cap and pulled it on.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted for his cap, found none, and covered his head with a groom's hat.

sentences.zh: 宣詔畢，頓首不能出聲，但言「吳昌時殺我」，乃就縊。

translations.literal: When the edict had been read he kowtowed but could not make a sound, only saying "Wu Changshi killed me," then went to the noose.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict he kowtowed wordlessly, cried "Wu Changshi killed me," and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 明日，使者還奏。

translations.literal: The next day the envoys returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the messengers reported back.

sentences.zh: 又明日許收斂，懸梁者兩日矣。

translations.literal: Only the day after was burial permitted; he had hung two days already.
translations.idiomatic: Burial was allowed only on the morrow—two days on the beam.

sentences.zh: 輔臣戮死，自世廟夏言後，此再見雲。

translations.literal: A grand minister put to death—since Xia Yan under the Emperor Shizong, this was seen again.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister executed—to be seen again only since Xia Yan in the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 法司坐其贓九千，沒入田六百畝，故宅一區。

translations.literal: The judiciary fixed his illicit gains at nine thousand taels, confiscated six hundred mu of fields, and one old residence.
translations.idiomatic: The law officers assessed nine thousand taels in graft, seized six hundred mu and one manor.

sentences.zh: 國觀險忮，然罪不至死，帝徒以私憤殺之，贓又懸坐，人頗有冤之者。

translations.literal: Guoguan was ruthless and jealous, yet his crime did not merit death; the emperor killed him from private rage alone, and the graft charges were inflated—many felt he had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan was vicious and spiteful, but death was excessive—the emperor slew him from private fury on trumped-up loot, and many called it injustice.

sentences.zh: 袁愷，聊城人。

translations.literal: Yuan Kai was a native of Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Kai came from Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 既劾罪國觀，後為給事中宋之普所傾，罷去。

translations.literal: After he had impeached and condemned Guoguan, he was later overturned by supervising secretary Song Zhipu and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Having ruined Guoguan, he was later undone by supervising secretary Song Zhipu and driven out.

sentences.zh: 福王時，起故官，道卒。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was restored to his old post and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Restored under the Prince of Fu, he died en route to office.

sentences.zh: 程國祥

translations.literal: Cheng Guoxiang
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Guoxiang

sentences.zh: 程國祥，字仲若，上元人。

translations.literal: Cheng Guoxiang, style name Zhongruo, was a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Guoxiang, styled Zhongruo, was from Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷三十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Wanli 32.

sentences.zh: 歷知確山、光山二縣，有清名。

translations.literal: He served in turn as magistrate of Queshan and Guangshan, winning a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Queshan and then Guangshan, he earned a name for clean rule.

sentences.zh: 遷南京吏部主事，乞養歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel and begged leave to nurse his parents and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to principal secretary at Nanjing Personnel, he sought leave to care for his parents and went home.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起禮部主事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled as principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned as a Rites principal secretary.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，吏部尚書趙南星知其可任，調為己屬，更歷四司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi, Minister of Personnel Zhao Nanxing, knowing him capable, transferred him to his own staff, and he passed through four bureaus in turn.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 4 Zhao Nanxing of Personnel, deeming him fit, pulled him onto his staff; he rotated through four bureaus.

sentences.zh: 發御史楊玉珂請屬，玉珂被謫，國祥亦引疾歸。

translations.literal: He exposed censor Yang Yuke's request for favoritism; Yuke was demoted and Guoxiang also pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He caught censor Yang Yuke soliciting favor; Yuke was banished and Guoxiang retired on illness.

sentences.zh: 其冬，魏忠賢既逐南星，御史張訥劾國祥為南星邪黨，遂除名。

translations.literal: That winter, after Wei Zhongxian had driven out Nanxing, censor Zhang Ne impeached Guoxiang as Nanxing's heterodox partisan, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, with Nanxing ousted by Wei Zhongxian, censor Zhang Ne branded Guoxiang a Nanxing partisan and erased his name.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，起稽勛員外郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was restored as vice director in the Bureau of Meritorious Service.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 2 restored him as vice director of meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 遷考功郎中，主外計，時稱公慎。

translations.literal: Promoted to director in the Bureau of Evaluation, he oversaw outer evaluations and was then praised as fair and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: As evaluation director overseeing provincial reviews, he was hailed for fairness.

sentences.zh: 御史龔守忠詆國祥通賄，國祥疏辯。

translations.literal: Censor Gong Shouzhong accused Guoxiang of bribery; Guoxiang memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gong Shouzhong charged him with graft; Guoxiang defended himself by memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝褒以清執，下都察院核奏，事得白，守忠坐褫官。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his clean conduct, sent the matter to the Censorate for verification and report, the affair was cleared, and Shouzhong was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his integrity, ordered the Censorate to investigate; he was cleared and Shouzhong dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋遷大理右寺丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice director of the Right Court of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became vice director at the Right Review Court.

sentences.zh: 歷太常卿、南京通政使，就遷工部侍郎，復調戶部。

translations.literal: He passed through Minister of Ceremonies and Transmission Commissioner at Nanjing, was then made Vice Minister of Works, and was transferred again to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Ceremonies and Nanjing transmission commissioner, became vice minister of Works, then moved to Revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年冬，召拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year nine he was summoned Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌議增餉，國祥不敢違。

translations.literal: Yang Sichang proposed increasing the surtax; Guoxiang dared not oppose it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang wanted higher levies; Guoxiang did not dare refuse.

sentences.zh: 而是時度支益匱，四方奏報災傷者相繼。

translations.literal: Yet at that time disbursements grew ever tighter, and reports of disaster and hardship from every quarter followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the treasury thinned while disaster reports flooded in from every province.

sentences.zh: 國祥多方區畫，亦時有所蠲減，最後建議，借都城賃舍一季租，可得五十萬，帝遂行之。

translations.literal: Guoxiang schemed on many sides and at times secured reductions; his final proposal was to borrow one quarter's rent on capital rental dwellings, yielding five hundred thousand taels, and the emperor carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxiang juggled accounts, sometimes winning remissions; finally he proposed seizing one season's rent on Beijing leaseholds—five hundred thousand taels—and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 勛戚奄豎悉隱匿不奏，所得僅十三萬，而怨聲載途。

translations.literal: Meritorious kin and eunuchs all concealed their holdings and did not report; only one hundred thirty thousand was obtained, while resentment filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and eunuchs hid their properties; only 130,000 came in—and outrage filled the streets.

sentences.zh: 然帝由是眷國祥。

translations.literal: Yet from this the emperor's favor toward Guoxiang grew.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the emperor's regard for Guoxiang deepened.

sentences.zh: 十一年六月，帝將增置閣臣，出禦中極殿，召廷臣七十余人親試之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eleventh year the emperor wished to add Grand Secretariat members; he went to the Central Apex Hall and summoned more than seventy court officials for a personal examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year eleven he meant to enlarge the secretariat, entered the Central Apex Hall, and personally tested seventy-odd officials.

sentences.zh: 發策言：「年來天災頻仍，今夏旱益甚，金星晝見五旬，四月山西大雪。

translations.literal: The examination topic read: "In recent years calamities have come in succession; this summer's drought is worse still. Venus appeared by day for fifty days; in the fourth month Shanxi saw heavy snow.
translations.idiomatic: The question ran: "Disasters multiply; this summer's drought is worse. Venus shone by day fifty days; Shanxi snowed in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 朝廷腹心耳目臣，務避嫌怨。

translations.literal: The court's closest ministers and eyes and ears shun suspicion and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's inner circle shuns blame.

sentences.zh: 有司舉劾，情賄關其心。

translations.literal: When officials impeach, sentiment and bribes sway their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Impeachments turn on favor and silver.

sentences.zh: 克期平賊無功，而剿兵難撤。

translations.literal: Deadlines to pacify bandits pass without success, yet suppression troops are hard to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit deadlines fail while suppression armies cannot come home.

sentences.zh: 外敵生心，邊餉日絀。

translations.literal: Outer enemies take heart; frontier pay shrinks day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign foes grow bold; border funds dwindle daily.

sentences.zh: 民貧既甚，正供猶艱。

translations.literal: The people are utterly impoverished, yet regular taxes remain hard to collect.
translations.idiomatic: The people are destitute; lawful dues are still hard to raise.

sentences.zh: 有司侵削百方，如火益熱。

translations.literal: Local officials squeeze by every means, adding fuel to fire.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates squeeze from every angle, heat upon heat.

sentences.zh: 若何處置得宜，禁戢有法，卿等悉心以對。」

translations.literal: How may matters be handled fittingly and excess restrained by law? You are to answer with all your hearts."
translations.idiomatic: How restore order and bind abuse by law? Answer with your whole mind."

sentences.zh: 會天大雨，諸臣面對後，漏已深，終考者止三十七人。

translations.literal: Just then heaven sent a great rain; after the officials faced the throne, the water clock was already deep into the night, and only thirty-seven finished the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell in torrents; after audiences the night was far gone—only thirty-seven completed the exam.

sentences.zh: 顧帝意已前定，特假是為名耳。

translations.literal: But the emperor's mind was already settled beforehand; he merely used this as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's choices were already made; the exam was theater.

sentences.zh: 居數日，改國祥禮部尚書，與楊嗣昌、方逢年、蔡國用、範復粹俱兼東閣大學士，入參機務。

translations.literal: Within days Guoxiang was made Minister of Rites, and together with Yang Sichang, Fang Fengnian, Cai Guoyong, and Fan Fuchun all served concurrently as Grand Secretaries of the Eastern Pavilion, entering to handle state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Guoxiang became Minister of Rites; with Yang Sichang, Fang Fengnian, Cai Guoyong, and Fan Fuchun he entered the Eastern Pavilion as grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 時劉宇亮為首輔，傅冠、薛國觀次之，又驟增國祥等五人。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Yuliang was chief minister, Fu Guan and Xue Guoguan next, and suddenly Guoxiang and five others were added.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuliang headed the cabinet, Fu Guan and Xue Guoguan followed—and five more, Guoxiang among them, were rushed in.

sentences.zh: 國觀、嗣昌最用事，國祥委蛇其間，自守而已。

translations.literal: Guoguan and Sichang held the most power; Guoxiang maneuvered among them and merely held himself in check.
translations.idiomatic: Guoguan and Sichang ruled; Guoxiang drifted between them and kept his head down.

sentences.zh: 明年四月召對，無一言。

translations.literal: The next year, at an audience called in the fourth month, he did not speak a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience in the fourth month of the next year, he said nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝傳諭責國祥緘默，大負委任，國祥遂乞休去。

translations.literal: The emperor sent word rebuking Guoxiang for silence, saying he had greatly failed his commission; Guoxiang thereupon begged leave to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rebuked his silence as betrayal of trust; Guoxiang asked to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 國祥始受業於焦竑，歷任卿相，布衣蔬食，不改儒素。

translations.literal: Guoxiang had first studied under Jiao Hong; though he rose to minister and chancellor, he wore plain cloth and ate simple food and did not change his scholar's austerity.
translations.idiomatic: A pupil of Jiao Hong, he reached the highest offices yet kept coarse cloth and plain fare.

sentences.zh: 與其子上俱撰有詩集。

translations.literal: He and his son Shang both compiled collections of poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He and his son Shang each left books of verse.

sentences.zh: 國祥歿後，家貧，不能舉火。

translations.literal: After Guoxiang died his household was so poor they could not kindle a cooking fire.
translations.idiomatic: When Guoxiang died his family was too poor to light a hearth.

sentences.zh: 上營葬畢，感疾卒，無嗣。

translations.literal: After arranging his father's burial, Shang fell ill and died, leaving no heir.
translations.idiomatic: Shang buried him, sickened, and died without sons.

sentences.zh: 蔡國用，金溪人。

translations.literal: Cai Guoyong was a native of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Guoyong came from Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Wanli 38.

sentences.zh: 由中書舍人擢御史。

translations.literal: From Secretariat Drafter he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from drafter to censor.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年陳時政六事，詆葉向高、趙南星，而薦亓詩教、趙興邦、邵輔忠、姚宗文等七人，魏忠賢喜，矯旨褒納。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi he memorialized on six current affairs, denouncing Ye Xianggao and Zhao Nanxing while recommending Qi Shijiao, Zhao Xingbang, Shao Fuzhong, Yao Zongwen, and seven others; Wei Zhongxian was pleased and by forged edict praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 5 he listed six policy points, attacked Ye Xianggao and Zhao Nanxing, praised Qi Shijiao, Zhao Xingbang, Shao Fuzhong, Yao Zongwen, and seven others; Wei Zhongxian forged an edict of approval.

sentences.zh: 尋忤珰意，勒令閑住。

translations.literal: Before long he offended the eunuch faction's intent and was ordered to idle appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he crossed the eunuchs and was sidelined.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年起故官，屢遷工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was restored to his old post and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Restored in Chongzhen 1, he rose to vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 督修都城，需石甚急，不克辦。

translations.literal: Supervising repairs to the capital walls, he urgently needed stone and could not supply it.
translations.idiomatic: Overseeing capital wall repairs, he needed stone urgently and could not meet the demand.

sentences.zh: 國用建議取牙石用之。

translations.literal: Guoyong proposed taking tooth-stone from the battlements for use.
translations.idiomatic: Guoyong proposed stripping merlon stone from the walls.

sentences.zh: 牙石者，舊列崇文、宣武兩街，備駕出除道者也。

translations.literal: “Tooth-merlons”—yashi—had long been arrayed along Chongwen and Xuanwu streets to clear the road when the imperial carriage went out.
translations.idiomatic: These ceremonial merlon stones had traditionally lined Chongwen and Xuanwu streets so the emperor’s procession could have the road cleared in advance.

sentences.zh: 帝閱城，嘉其功，遂欲大用。

translations.literal: The emperor inspected the walls, praised his achievement, and wished to employ him on a grander scale.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the fortifications, he applauded the work and resolved to promote Guoyong to greater responsibility.

sentences.zh: 十一年六月，廷推閣臣，國用望輕，不獲與，特旨擢禮部尚書，入閣辦事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eleventh year, when the court recommended Grand Secretaries, Guoyong’s standing was slight and he was not included; by special edict he was promoted to Minister of Rites and entered the Grand Secretariat to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Chongzhen 11, court nomination for the Grand Secretariat passed him over as a lightweight; the throne then singled him out for Minister of Rites and a seat in the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 累加少保，改吏部尚書、武英殿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Junior Guardian, and his post was changed to Minister of Personnel and the Hall of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Further honors made him Junior Guardian; he was reassigned as Minister of Personnel with a seat in the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 十三年六月卒於官，贈太保，謚文恪。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year he died in office; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the sixth month of Chongzhen 13 and was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the temple name Wenge.

sentences.zh: 國用居位清謹，與同列張四知皆庸才，碌碌無所見。

translations.literal: Guoyong was scrupulous and cautious in office; he and his colleague Zhang Sizhi were both mediocre talents who achieved nothing of note.
translations.idiomatic: Guoyong served with sober integrity, but he and fellow Grand Secretary Zhang Sizhi were undistinguished men who left no mark on policy.

sentences.zh: 範復粹，黃縣人。

translations.literal: Fan Fuchun was a native of Huang County.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Fuchun came from Huang County.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十七年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in Wanli 47.

sentences.zh: 除開封府推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was as investigating censor in Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年為御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he became a censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 he entered the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 廷議移毛文龍內地，復粹言：「海外億萬生靈誰非赤子，倘棲身無所，必各據一島為盜，後患方深。」

translations.literal: The court debated moving Mao Wenlong inland; Fuchun said: “Of the tens of millions living beyond the sea, who is not the emperor’s child? If they have nowhere to dwell, each will seize an island and turn pirate—the trouble afterward will run deep.”
translations.idiomatic: When the court weighed relocating Mao Wenlong inland, Fuchun said, "Of the tens of millions living beyond the sea, who is not the emperor's child? If they have nowhere to dwell, each will seize an island and turn pirate—the trouble afterward will run deep."

sentences.zh: 又言：「袁崇煥功在全遼，而尚寶卿董懋中詆為逆黨所庇，持論狂謬。」

translations.literal: He also said: “Yuan Chonghuan’s merit lay in securing all Liaodong, yet Court of Imperial Sacrifices Director Dong Maozhong slandered him as shielded by traitor factions—his position was wildly absurd.”
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Yuan Chonghuan's merit lay in securing all Liaodong, yet Court of Imperial Sacrifices Director Dong Maozhong slandered him as shielded by traitor factions—his position was wildly absurd."

sentences.zh: 懋中遂落職，文龍亦不果移。

translations.literal: Maozhong was thereupon dismissed from office, and Wenlong was not moved after all.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Maozhong lost his post, and Mao Wenlong was never relocated.

sentences.zh: 巡按江西，請禁有司害民六事。

translations.literal: Touring as investigating censor in Jiangxi, he petitioned to forbid six kinds of harm inflicted on the people by local officials.
translations.idiomatic: On provincial inspection in Jiangxi, he asked the throne to ban six abuses by local magistrates against the people.

sentences.zh: 時大厘郵傳積弊，減削過甚，反累民，復粹極陳不便。

translations.literal: At the time a great purge of abuses in the courier system cut too deep and instead burdened the people; Fuchun strongly argued that this was impractical.
translations.idiomatic: When reforms of the postal relay system slashed costs so sharply that commoners suffered, Fuchun pressed the emperor that the cuts were unworkable.

sentences.zh: 丁艱歸。

translations.literal: He returned home upon the death of a parent.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，還朝，出按陜西。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he returned to court and went out to inspect Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he resumed duty and toured Shaanxi as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 陳治標治本之策：以任將、設防、留餉為治標；

translations.literal: He set out policies to treat symptoms and root causes: appointing generals, building defenses, and retaining grain pay as treating symptoms;
translations.idiomatic: He framed both urgent and lasting remedies—generals, fortifications, and retained rations as immediate measures;

sentences.zh: 廣屯、蠲賦、招撫為治本。

translations.literal: expanding military colonies, remitting taxes, and winning people back by conciliation as treating root causes.
translations.idiomatic: while expanded garrison farming, tax relief, and pacification through settlement would strike at the roots.

sentences.zh: 帝褒納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended the plan and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 廷議有司督賦缺額，兼罪撫按，復粹力言不可。

translations.literal: When the court debated holding provincial officials liable for shortfalls in tax collection and punishing governors and surveillance commissioners jointly, Fuchun forcefully argued that this must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He fought a proposal to punish governors and surveillance commissioners whenever local officials missed tax quotas.

sentences.zh: 由大理右寺丞進左少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted from Right Assistant Director of the Court of the Great Canon to Left Vice Minister of the same court.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from right assistant director to left vice minister in the Court of the Great Canon.

sentences.zh: 居無何，超拜禮部左侍郎兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was abruptly promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was leapfrogged to Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時同命者五人，翰林惟方逢年，余皆外僚，而復粹由少卿，尤屬異數。

translations.literal: At that time five men received the same appointment; among Hanlin scholars only Fang Fengnian was included—the rest were outsiders—and Fuchun’s jump from vice minister was especially unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Five were named together; only Fang Fengnian among them came from the Hanlin, the others from outside, and Fuchun’s promotion straight from a vice ministership was a singular honor.

sentences.zh: 蓋帝欲閣臣通知六部事，故每部簡一人：首輔劉宇亮由吏部，國祥以戶，逢年以禮，嗣昌以兵，國用以工，刑部無人，復粹以大理代之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished Grand Secretaries to understand the business of the Six Ministries, so one man was chosen from each ministry: Chief Grand Secretary Liu Yuliang from Personnel; Guoxiang from Revenue; Fengnian from Rites; Sichang from War; Guoyong from Works; no one from Punishments—Fuchun from the Court of the Great Canon filled that gap.
translations.idiomatic: The throne wanted cabinet ministers versed in every ministry, so each ministry supplied one man—Liu Yuliang from Personnel, Guoxiang from Revenue, Fengnian from Rites, Sichang from War, Guoyong from Works—while Fuchun, from the judiciary side at the Court of the Great Canon, stood in for Punishments.

sentences.zh: 累加少保，進吏部尚書、武英殿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Junior Guardian and advanced to Minister of Personnel and the Hall of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Further honors made him Junior Guardian, then Minister of Personnel in the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 十三年六月，國觀罷，復粹為首輔。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year, when Guo Guan was dismissed, Fuchun became chief Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Guan’s dismissal in the sixth month of Chongzhen 13, Fuchun became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 給事中黃雲師言「宰相須才識度三者」，復粹恚，因自陳三者無一，請罷，溫旨慰留。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Huang Yunshi said that “a prime minister must possess talent, knowledge, and breadth”; Fuchun was enraged, declared in a memorial that he lacked all three, and asked to be dismissed, but a warm edict comforted him and kept him in place.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Yunshi wrote that "a prime minister must possess talent, insight, and breadth," Fuchun—furious—confessed he had none of the three and begged to resign; the emperor soothed him and refused.

sentences.zh: 御史魏景琦劾復粹及張四知學淺才疏，伴食中書，遺譏海內。

translations.literal: Censor Wei Jingqi impeached Fuchun and Zhang Sizhi as shallow in learning and weak in talent—empty placeholders in the Secretariat who brought ridicule throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wei Jingqi attacked Fuchun and Zhang Sizhi as learned only in name, useless at the drafting table, and a laughingstock nationwide.

sentences.zh: 帝以妄詆下之吏。

translations.literal: The emperor, deeming this reckless slander, handed him over to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: The throne treated the charge as malicious libel and sent Wei Jingqi to the courts.

sentences.zh: 明年，加少傅兼太子太傅，改建極殿。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and moved to the Hall of Establishing the Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received junior tutor and heir-apparent tutor titles and a seat in the Hall of Establishing the Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 賊陷洛陽，復粹等引罪乞罷，不允。

translations.literal: When bandits took Luoyang, Fuchun and others took blame and begged to resign; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: After rebels captured Luoyang, Fuchun and colleagues offered their resignations; the emperor declined.

sentences.zh: 帝御乾清宮左室，召對廷臣，語及福王被害，泣下。

translations.literal: The emperor received the court in the left chamber of the Palace of Heavenly Purity, summoned ministers for audience, spoke of the Prince of Fu’s murder, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: In the left annex of the Palace of Heavenly Purity the emperor held audience, spoke of the slain Prince of Fu, and broke into tears.

sentences.zh: 復粹曰：「此乃天數。」

translations.literal: Fuchun said: "This is Heaven's decree."
translations.idiomatic: Fuchun replied, "This was fate."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「雖氣數，亦賴人事挽回。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: “Even if it is the turn of fortune, human effort can still turn it back.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, “Even cosmic cycles can be bent back by what men do.”

sentences.zh: 復粹等不能對。

translations.literal: Fuchun and the others could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchun and his colleagues had nothing to say.

sentences.zh: 帝疾初愈，大赦天下，命復粹錄囚，自尚書傅宗龍以下，多所減免。

translations.literal: When the emperor had just recovered from illness, he proclaimed a general amnesty and ordered Fuchun to review prisoners; from Minister Fu Zonglong downward many sentences were reduced or remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from illness the emperor declared a great amnesty and had Fuchun review cases, commuting punishments from Minister Fu Zonglong on down.

sentences.zh: 是年五月致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned in the fifth month of that year.

sentences.zh: 國變後，卒於家。

translations.literal: After the dynastic collapse he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home after the fall of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 方逢年，遂安人。

translations.literal: Fang Fengnian was a native of Suian.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fengnian came from Suian.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Wanli 44.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，以編修典湖廣試，發策有「巨珰大蠹」語，且雲「宇內豈無人焉？

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi, as compiler he presided over the Huguang provincial examination; his policy question contained the phrase “giant eunuchs, great parasites,” and also asked, “Is there truly no talent under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 4, supervising the Huguang exams as a compiler, he set a policy theme denouncing “giant eunuchs and great parasites” and asked whether the empire truly lacked able men.

sentences.zh: 有薄士大夫而覓臯、夔、稷、契於黃衣閹尹之流者」。

translations.literal: Are there those who slight the scholar-official class yet seek a Gao Yao, a Qi, a Ji, or a Xie among the yellow-robed palace eunuchs?”
translations.idiomatic: Are there those who slight the scholar-official class yet seek a Gao Yao, a Qi, a Ji, or a Xie among the yellow-robed palace eunuchs?"

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢見之，怒，貶三秩調外。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian saw this, grew angry, and demoted him three ranks and transferred him outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian read the papers, flew into a rage, stripped him of three ranks, and sent him into provincial exile.

sentences.zh: 御史徐復陽希指劾之，削籍為民。

translations.literal: Censor Xu Fuyang, currying favor, impeached him and had his name struck from the rolls, reducing him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xu Fuyang, eager to please, impeached him and had him expelled from the register as a private citizen.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起原官，累遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was restored to his former post and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzhen began he was reinstated and rose to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十一年詔廷臣舉邊才，逢年以汪喬年應。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict ordered court officials to recommend frontier talent; Fengnian nominated Wang Qiaonian.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 11 the throne called for border experts; Fengnian recommended Wang Qiaonian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢禮部尚書，入閣輔政。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Minister of Rites and entered the Grand Secretariat to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Minister of Rites and joined the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 其冬，刑科奏摘參未完疏，逢年以犯贓私者，人亡產絕，親戚坐累，幾同瓜蔓，遂輕擬以上。

translations.literal: That winter the Office of Scrutiny for Punishments reported unfinished memorials calling out officials; Fengnian held that when the guilty were dead and their estates exhausted, kin punished by association nearly amounted to guilt by extension—so he lightly proposed approval.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the punishment scrutiny office listed pending impeachments; Fengnian argued that punishing relatives when the corrupt official was dead and penniless smacked of collective guilt, and he leaned toward lenient approval.

sentences.zh: 而帝意欲罪刑部尚書劉之鳳，責逢年疏忽。

translations.literal: But the emperor wished to punish Minister of Punishments Liu Zhifeng and blamed Fengnian for negligence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, intent on punishing Minister Liu Zhifeng, faulted Fengnian for carelessness.

sentences.zh: 逢年引罪，即罷歸。

translations.literal: Fengnian took blame and was at once dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Fengnian accepted blame and was immediately dismissed.

sentences.zh: 福王時，復原官，不召。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu his old post was restored, but he was not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu restored his rank but never called him back.

sentences.zh: 魯王三召之，用其議，定稱魯監國。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu summoned him three times, adopted his proposal, and fixed the title of Lu as regent.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu summoned him thrice, followed his advice, and settled on the style “Regent of Lu.”

sentences.zh: 紹興破，王航海，逢年追不及，與方國安等降於我大清。

translations.literal: When Shaoxing fell the prince put to sea; Fengnian could not catch up and surrendered with Fang Guoan and others to Our Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaoxing fell the prince fled by sea; Fengnian failed to follow and surrendered with Fang Guoan and others to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 已而以蠟丸書通閩，事泄被誅。

translations.literal: Later he used a wax-sealed letter to communicate with Min; when the plot leaked he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He later tried to reach the Fujian court with a wax-sealed message; discovery of the plot brought his execution.

sentences.zh: 張四知者，費縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Sizhi was a native of Fei County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sizhi came from Fei County.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in Tianqi 2.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士授檢討。

translations.literal: From Hanlin bachelor he was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hanlin academy he served as reviser.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，歷官禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Under Chongzhen he rose to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen reign he became Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 貌寢甚，嘗患惡瘍。

translations.literal: His appearance was very homely, and he once suffered from a foul ulcer.
translations.idiomatic: He was remarkably plain in face and had once been afflicted with a noisome sore.

sentences.zh: 十一年六月，廷推閣臣忽及之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eleventh year, when the court recommended Grand Secretaries, he was suddenly included.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Chongzhen 11 court nomination for the cabinet suddenly named him.

sentences.zh: 給事中張淳劾其為祭酒時貪汙狀，四知憤，帝前力辨，言己孤立，為廷臣所嫉。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Chun impeached his corrupt conduct while Grand Preceptor of the National University; Sizhi, indignant, forcefully argued before the emperor that he stood alone and was envied by court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Chun accused him of graft as university chancellor; Sizhi, furious, told the emperor he was isolated and hated by his peers.

sentences.zh: 帝意頗動，薛國觀因力援之。

translations.literal: The emperor’s mind was somewhat moved; Xue Guoguan therefore strongly supported him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wavered, and Xue Guoguan pressed hard on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 明年五月與姚明恭、魏照乘俱拜禮部尚書兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year he, Yao Minggong, and Wei Zhaocheng were all appointed Ministers of Rites and Grand Secretaries of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The following fifth month he, Yao Minggong, and Wei Zhaocheng all became Ministers of Rites and Eastern Pavilion grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 明恭，蘄水人。

translations.literal: Minggong was a native of Qishui.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Minggong came from Qishui.

sentences.zh: 出趙興邦門，公論素不予。

translations.literal: He came from Zhao Xingbang’s faction; public opinion had never favored him.
translations.idiomatic: A protégé of Zhao Xingbang, he had long lacked public esteem.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十一年，由詹事遷禮部侍郎，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chongzhen he moved from Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent to Vice Minister of Rites and instructor of Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 11 he went from heir-apparent tutor to Vice Minister of Rites and mentor of Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 給事中耿始然劾其與副都御史袁鯨比而為奸利，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Geng Shiran impeached him and Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuan Jing for colluding in illicit profit; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Geng Shiran accused him and Vice Censor Yuan Jing of profiteering together; the throne ignored it.

sentences.zh: 明年遂柄用。

translations.literal: The next year he was put in power.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was brought into the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 照乘，滑人。

translations.literal: Zhaocheng was a native of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaocheng came from Hua.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，為吏部都給事中。

translations.literal: Under Tianqi he was supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi era he served as supervising secretary in Personnel.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十一年，歷官兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chongzhen he rose to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: By Chongzhen 11 he was Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，國觀引入閣。

translations.literal: The next year Guoguan brought him into the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Guoguan installed him in the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 三人者，皆庸劣充位而已。

translations.literal: The three men were all mediocre talents merely filling their posts.
translations.idiomatic: All three were undistinguished men who held office only in name.

sentences.zh: 四知加太子太保，進吏部尚書、武英殿。

translations.literal: Sizhi was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, advanced to Minister of Personnel and the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and promoted Minister of Personnel in the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 明恭加太子太保，進戶部尚書、文淵閣。

translations.literal: Minggong was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, advanced to Minister of Revenue and the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Minggong was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and promoted Minister of Revenue in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 照乘加太子少傅，進戶部尚書、文淵閣。

translations.literal: Zhaocheng was made Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, advanced to Minister of Revenue and the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocheng was made Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and promoted Minister of Revenue in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝自即位，務抑言官，不欲以其言斥免大臣。

translations.literal: Since his accession the emperor had striven to suppress the censorate and did not wish to dismiss grand ministers on their word.
translations.idiomatic: From his accession the emperor sought to curb the remonstrating officials and would not remove senior ministers at their urging.

sentences.zh: 彈章愈多，位愈固。

translations.literal: The more impeachments, the firmer their positions.
translations.idiomatic: The more they were impeached, the more secure their posts became.

sentences.zh: 四知秉政四載，為給事中馬嘉植，御史鄭昆貞、曹溶等所劾，帝皆不納，十五年六月始致仕。

translations.literal: Sizhi held power four years and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Ma Jiazhi and Censors Zheng Kunzhen and Cao Rong, among others; the emperor accepted none of it, and only in the sixth month of the fifteenth year did Sizhi retire.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi governed four years; Ma Jiazhi and Censors Zheng Kunzhen and Cao Rong impeached him repeatedly, but the emperor rejected every charge, and Sizhi retired only in the sixth month of Chongzhen 15.

sentences.zh: 照乘亦四載，御史楊仁願、徐殿臣、劉之渤相繼論劾，引疾去。

translations.literal: Zhaocheng likewise four years; Censors Yang Renyuan, Xu Dianchen, and Liu Zhibo impeached him in succession, and he cited illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocheng also served four years; Censors Yang Renyuan, Xu Dianchen, and Liu Zhibo attacked him one after another, and he pleaded illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明恭甫一載，鄉人詣闕訟之，請告歸。

translations.literal: Minggong had been in office only a year when his fellow townsmen went to the court to plead against him; he asked leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Minggong had barely served a year when neighbors from Qishui petitioned at court against him; he sought leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 後四知降於我大清。

translations.literal: Later Sizhi surrendered to our Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sizhi submitted to the Great Qing.

sentences.zh: 陳演，井研人。

translations.literal: Chen Yan was a native of Jingyan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan came from Jingyan.

sentences.zh: 祖效，萬歷間以御史監征倭軍，卒於朝鮮，贈光祿卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiao, who in the Wanli era as censor supervised troops levied against the Japanese Wokou, died in Korea and was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiao, a Wanli-era censor who oversaw anti-Wokou levies, died in Korea and was posthumously made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 演登天啟二年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Yan passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tianqi, entered the Hanlin as bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Yan took jinshi in Tianqi 2, joined the Hanlin as bachelor, and became compiler.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，歷官少詹事，掌翰林院，直講筵。

translations.literal: Under Chongzhen he served as Junior Grand Secretary, directed the Hanlin Academy, and lectured at the classic exposition.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen he was junior grand secretary, headed the Hanlin Academy, and lectured before the throne.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，擢禮部右侍郎，協理詹事府。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites and assisted in managing the Grand Preceptorate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongzhen 13 he became Vice Minister of Rites and helped run the heir-apparent’s household.

sentences.zh: 演庸才寡學，工結納。

translations.literal: Yan was a mediocre talent of shallow learning, skilled at cultivating connections.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan was a man of little learning and ordinary ability, adept at networking.

sentences.zh: 初入館，即與內侍通。

translations.literal: As soon as he entered the academy he was on familiar terms with inner eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: From his first days in the Hanlin he cultivated palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝簡用閣臣，每親發策，以所條對覘能否。

translations.literal: When Emperor Sizong selected Grand Secretaries, he personally set policy questions to test their answers and judge their capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Sizong, choosing cabinet ministers, personally drafted policy questions to probe their competence.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，中官探得帝所欲問數事，密授演，條對獨稱旨，即拜禮部左侍郎兼東閣大學士，與謝升同入閣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year palace eunuchs learned several questions the emperor intended to ask, secretly passed them to Yan, and his written replies alone pleased the throne; he was at once made Left Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the Grand Secretariat together with Xie Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: That fourth month eunuchs learned what the emperor would ask, tipped Yan off, and only his answers satisfied the throne—he was instantly made Vice Minister of Rites and Eastern Pavilion grand secretary alongside Xie Sheng.

sentences.zh: 明年，進禮部尚書，改文淵閣。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Minister of Rites and moved to the Hall of Literary Depth.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Minister of Rites in the Hall of Literary Depth.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以山東平盜功加太子少保，改戶部尚書、武英殿。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, for merit in pacifying bandits in Shandong he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and his post was changed to Minister of Revenue and the Hall of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 15, rewarded for quelling Shandong bandits, he became junior tutor to the heir apparent and Minister of Revenue in the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 被劾乞罷，優旨慰留。

translations.literal: Impeached, he begged to resign; a gracious edict comforted him and kept him in place.
translations.idiomatic: After impeachment he asked to quit; a kind edict refused and kept him at post.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，周延儒去位，遂為首輔。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year, when Zhou Yanru left office, he became chief Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The next fifth month, after Zhou Yanru’s departure, he became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 尋以城守功，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon, for merit in defending the city, he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, for defending the capital, he was made grand tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月考滿，加少保，改吏部尚書、建極殿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year, when his term review was complete, he was made Junior Guardian and his post changed to Minister of Personnel and the Hall of Establishing the Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongzhen 17, at the end of his evaluation cycle, he became Junior Guardian and Minister of Personnel in the Hall of Establishing the Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 逾月罷政。

translations.literal: More than a month later he left government.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he was dismissed from power.

sentences.zh: 再逾月，都城陷，遂及於難。

translations.literal: Another month on, the capital fell, and he met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Another month after that the city fell, and he perished in the catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 演為人既庸且刻。

translations.literal: Yan was by nature both mediocre and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan was at once dull and cruel.

sentences.zh: 惡副都御史房可壯、河南道張煊不受屬，因會推閣臣讒於帝，可壯等六人俱下吏。

translations.literal: He hated Vice Censor-in-Chief Fang Kezhuang and Henan Circuit censor Zhang Xuan for refusing his patronage; at a joint recommendation for Grand Secretaries he slandered them to the emperor, and Kezhuang and five others were all handed to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Resenting Fang Kezhuang and Zhang Xuan for spurning his influence, he poisoned the emperor’s ear during a cabinet nomination, and six men including Fang were arrested.

sentences.zh: 王應熊召至，旋放還，演有力焉。

translations.literal: Wang Yingxiong was summoned to court and then released and sent back—Yan had exerted force in this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingxiong was called to the capital and then sent home again, largely through Yan’s pull.

sentences.zh: 自延儒罷後，帝最倚信演。

translations.literal: After Yanru’s dismissal the emperor relied on and trusted Yan most.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhou Yanru was gone, the emperor trusted Chen Yan above all other ministers.

sentences.zh: 臺省附延儒者，盡趨演門。

translations.literal: Those in the censorate and provincial offices who had attached themselves to Yanru all rushed to Yan’s door.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and officials who had clustered around Zhou Yanru now flocked to Chen Yan.

sentences.zh: 當是時，國勢累卵，中外舉知其不支。

translations.literal: At that time the state’s situation was as fragile as a piled egg; inside and outside the court all knew it could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty teetered like eggs stacked on one another; everyone knew collapse was near.

sentences.zh: 演無所籌畫，顧以賄聞。

translations.literal: Yan made no plans whatsoever, yet was known for taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan offered no strategy at all and was notorious for graft.

sentences.zh: 及李自成陷陜西，逼山西，廷議撤寧遠吳三桂兵入守山海關，策應京師。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng took Shaanxi and pressed on Shanxi, the court debated withdrawing Wu Sangui’s army from Ningyuan to guard Shanhai Pass and support the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Zicheng overran Shaanxi and threatened Shanxi, ministers debated pulling Wu Sangui’s garrison from Ningyuan to hold Shanhaiguan and relieve Beijing.

sentences.zh: 帝意亦然之，演持不可。

translations.literal: The emperor’s mind likewise favored this, but Yan held that it must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed in principle, but Chen Yan objected.

sentences.zh: 後帝決計行之，三桂始用海船渡遼民入關，往返者再，而賊已陷宣、大矣。

translations.literal: Later the emperor decided to carry it out; Sangui first used sea ships to ferry Liaodong people into the pass, making the round trip twice, and by then the bandits had already taken Xuanfu and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor finally ordered it, Wu Sangui began ferrying Liaodong refugees through Shanhaiguan by sea—twice across the waters—while the rebels were already seizing Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 演懼不自安，引疾求罷。

translations.literal: Yan feared and was not at ease; citing illness, he sought dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy and afraid, Chen Yan pleaded illness and asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 詔許之，賜道里費五十金，彩幣四表裏，乘傳行。

translations.literal: An edict granted it, bestowing fifty taels for road expenses, four sets of colored silks inside and out, and travel by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented, giving him fifty taels for the journey, four bundles of ceremonial silk, and post-horses to carry him home.

sentences.zh: 演既謝事，薊遼總督王永吉上疏力詆其罪，請置之典刑，給事中汪惟效、孫承澤亦極論之。

translations.literal: Once Yan had resigned, Jili-Liaodong Governor Wang Yongji memorialized forcefully denouncing his crimes and asking that he be subjected to statutory punishment; supervising secretaries Wang Weixiao and Sun Chengyze also argued to the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had Chen Yan stepped down when the Jili-Liaodong governor Wang Yongji memorialized in fierce condemnation, demanding the full penalty of the law; the supervising secretaries Wang Weixiao and Sun Chengyze joined the attack with equal vehemence.

sentences.zh: 演入辭，謂佐理無狀，罪當死。

translations.literal: Yan entered to take leave, saying that his assistance in governing had been worthless and his crime deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yan came to bid farewell, he admitted he had governed without merit and deserved death.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「汝一死不足蔽辜！」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Your single death is insufficient to cover your guilt!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blazed with anger: "One death from you would not atone for your sins!"

sentences.zh: 叱之去。

translations.literal: He shouted at him to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He drove him out with a rebuke.

sentences.zh: 演貲多，不能遽行。

translations.literal: Yan had much wealth and could not promptly depart.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan was too wealthy to leave in haste—there was too much to gather and move.

sentences.zh: 賊陷京師，與魏藻德等俱被執，系賊將劉宗敏營中。

translations.literal: When bandits took the capital, together with Wei Zaode and others he was seized and confined in the camp of the bandit general Liu Zongmin.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels seized Beijing, he was taken along with Wei Zaode and held in the camp of the rebel general Liu Zongmin.

sentences.zh: 其日獻銀四萬，賊喜，不加刑。

translations.literal: That day he presented forty thousand taels of silver; the bandits were pleased and did not apply torture.
translations.idiomatic: He handed over forty thousand taels of silver that day; the rebels were delighted and spared him torture.

sentences.zh: 四月八日，已得釋。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the fourth month, he had already been released.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighth day of the fourth month he had already been freed.

sentences.zh: 十二日，自成將東禦三桂，慮諸大臣為後患，盡殺之。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day, Zicheng was about to go east to meet San Gui and, fearing the various grand ministers would be a later calamity, killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth, as Li Zicheng prepared to march east against Wu Sangui, he feared the captive ministers would trouble him afterward and had them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 演亦遇害。

translations.literal: Yan also met with calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan perished among them.

sentences.zh: 魏藻德

translations.literal: Wei Zaode
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zaode

sentences.zh: 魏藻德，順天通州人。

translations.literal: Wei Zaode was a man of Tongzhou in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zaode came from Tongzhou in the Shuntian jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十三年舉進士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the thirteenth year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 既殿試，帝思得異才，復召四十八人於文華殿，問：「今日內外交訌，何以報仇雪恥？」

translations.literal: After the palace examination, the emperor, thinking to obtain exceptional talent, again summoned forty-eight men to the Wenhua Hall and asked: "Today internal and external troubles cross; how may we avenge and wipe away shame?"
translations.idiomatic: After the palace examination the emperor, hungering for extraordinary talent, summoned forty-eight candidates back to the Wenhua Hall and asked, "The realm is torn within and without—how shall we avenge our wrongs and wash away our disgrace?"

sentences.zh: 藻德即以「知恥」對，又自敘十一年守通州功。

translations.literal: Zaode immediately answered with "knowing shame," and furthermore narrated his own merits in defending Tongzhou for eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zaode answered with a single phrase—"know shame"—and went on to recount how he had held Tongzhou for eleven years.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，擢置第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, elevated him to first place, and appointed him compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, ranked him first, and made him a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 十五年，都城戒嚴，疏陳兵事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when the capital was placed under martial alert, he memorialized setting forth military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, as the capital went on war footing, he submitted a memorial on military matters.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，召對稱旨。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, summoned to audience, his answers accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the third month, his answers in a private audience delighted the emperor.

sentences.zh: 藻德有口才。

translations.literal: Zaode had a gift for speech.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zaode was a fluent and persuasive speaker.

sentences.zh: 帝以己所親擢，且意其有抱負，五月，驟擢禮部右侍郎兼東閣大學士，入閣輔政。

translations.literal: Because the emperor had personally elevated him and supposed he harbored ambition, in the fifth month he was suddenly promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the cabinet to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had raised him by his own hand and believed him capable; in the fifth month he was abruptly made Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, joining the inner cabinet.

sentences.zh: 藻德力辭部銜，乃改少詹事。

translations.literal: Zaode forcefully declined the ministry title, whereupon he was changed to Junior Supervisor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zaode vigorously refused the ministry rank and was given the post of Junior Supervisor of the Heir Apparent instead.

sentences.zh: 正統末年，兵事孔棘，彭時以殿試第一人，逾年即入閣，然仍故官修撰，未有超拜大學士者。

translations.literal: In the late Zhengtong era, when military affairs were urgently pressing, Peng Shi, first in the palace examination, entered the cabinet after a year yet still kept his former post as compiler; never before had one been leap-promoted to grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the crises of late Zhengtong, Peng Shi had entered the cabinet a year after topping the palace exam but still served as a mere compiler—no one had ever vaulted straight to grand secretary until now.

sentences.zh: 陳演見帝遇之厚，曲相比附。

translations.literal: Chen Yan saw that the emperor treated him generously and bent to align and attach himself.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's extraordinary favor, Chen Yan curried his alliance.

sentences.zh: 八月，補行會試引為副總裁，越蔣德璟、黃景昉而用之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, when the deferred metropolitan examination was held, he was made associate chief examiner, passed over Jiang Dejing and Huang Jingfang to use him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was named associate chief examiner for the deferred metropolitan exam, leapfrogging Jiang Dejing and Huang Jingfang.

sentences.zh: 藻德居位，一無建白，但倡議令百官捐助而已。

translations.literal: While Zaode held position, he made not a single constructive proposal, only initiating discussion for the hundred officials to contribute donations.
translations.idiomatic: As grand secretary, Wei Zaode offered no policy of substance—only a chorus calling on every official to donate funds.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月，詔加兵部尚書兼工部尚書、文淵閣大學士，總督河道、屯田、練兵諸事，駐天津，而命方嶽貢駐濟寧，蓋欲出太子南京，俾先清道路也。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year, an edict added Minister of War and Minister of Works and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, overseeing river works, garrison fields, and troop training, stationed at Tianjin, while Fang Yuegong was ordered stationed at Jining—generally intending to send the crown prince to Nanjing and have them first clear the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year he was made Minister of War, Minister of Works, and Wenyuan Grand Secretary, charged with rivers, garrison agriculture, and training troops at Tianjin, while Fang Yuegong was posted at Jining—the plan being to move the crown prince to Nanjing and secure the route ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 有言百官不可令出，出即潛遁者，遂止不行。

translations.literal: Some said the hundred officials must not be ordered out, for once out they would secretly flee; thereupon it stopped and was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Critics warned that officials sent away would simply abscond, and the scheme was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 及演罷，藻德遂為首輔。

translations.literal: When Yan was dismissed, Zaode then became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Yan's fall, Wei Zaode became chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 同事者李建泰、方嶽貢、範景文、邱瑜，皆新入政府，莫能補救。
