translations.literal: His colleagues were Li Jiantai, Fang Yuegong, Fan Jingwen, and Qiu Yu—all newly entered into government, none able to remedy matters.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues were Li Jiantai, Fang Yuegong, Fan Jingwen, and Qiu Yu, all fresh to power and none able to stanch the bleeding.

sentences.zh: 至三月，都城陷，景文死之，藻德、嶽貢、瑜並被執，幽劉宗敏所。

translations.literal: By the third month the capital fell; Jingwen died for the dynasty, while Zaode, Yuegong, and Yu were all seized and confined at Liu Zongmin's place.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell in the third month, Fan Jingwen died loyal to the throne; Wei Zaode, Fang Yuegong, and Qiu Yu were taken and held by Liu Zongmin.

sentences.zh: 賊下令勒內閣十萬金，京卿、錦衣七萬，或五三萬，給事、御史、吏部、翰林五萬至一萬有差，部曹數千，勛戚無定數。

translations.literal: The bandits ordered levies: the inner cabinet one hundred thousand taels, capital ministers and the Embroidered Uniform Guard seventy thousand or fifty or thirty thousand, supervising secretaries, censors, the Ministry of Personnel, and Hanlin from fifty thousand down to ten thousand by rank, ministry clerks several thousand, meritorious kin without fixed amount.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels set ransoms: one hundred thousand taels from the inner cabinet, seventy or fifty or thirty thousand from capital ministers and the Embroidered Uniform Guard, supervising secretaries, censors, the Ministry of Personnel, and Hanlin scholars from fifty thousand down to ten thousand by rank, ministry clerks in the thousands, and no fixed sum for imperial in-laws.

sentences.zh: 藻德輸萬金，賊以為少，酷刑五日夜，腦裂而死。

translations.literal: Zaode paid ten thousand taels; the bandits thought it too little and tortured him cruelly for five days and nights until his skull split and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zaode paid ten thousand taels; the rebels deemed it miserly and tortured him for five days and nights until his skull split and he died.

sentences.zh: 復逮其子追征，訴言：「家已罄盡。

translations.literal: They again seized his son to pursue collection; he pleaded, saying: "The house is already utterly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: They seized his son to squeeze out more; the son pleaded, "Our house is stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 父在，猶可丐諸門生故舊。

translations.literal: While my father lived, one could still beg among his students and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: While my father lived we could still beg his students and old friends.

sentences.zh: 今已死，復何所貸？」

translations.literal: Now that he is dead, from whom may we borrow?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is dead, who would lend us anything?"

sentences.zh: 賊揮刃斬之。

translations.literal: The bandits swung blades and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels cut him down with their blades.

sentences.zh: 李建泰

translations.literal: Li Jiantai
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiantai

sentences.zh: 李建泰，曲沃人。

translations.literal: Li Jiantai was a man of Quwo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiantai came from Quwo.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi he passed as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 歷官國子祭酒，頗著聲望。

translations.literal: He served as Chancellor of the Imperial Academy and won considerable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy and enjoyed a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年五月，擢吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen he was promoted to Vice Minister of the right in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Chongzhen sixteen he was made Vice Minister of the right in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以本官兼東閣大學士，與方嶽貢並命。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, with his former post he was also made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, appointed together with Fang Yuegong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was named Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion while keeping his ministry post, appointed alongside Fang Yuegong.

sentences.zh: 疏陳時政切要十事，帝皆允行。

translations.literal: He memorialized ten urgent points of current policy; the emperor approved them all for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on ten pressing reforms, and the emperor approved every one.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，李自成逼山西。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Li Zicheng pressed on Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the first month, Li Zicheng threatened Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 建泰慮鄉邦被禍，而家富於貲，可藉以佐軍，毅然有滅賊誌，常與同官言之。

translations.literal: Jiantai feared his home region would suffer calamity, and his family was rich in wealth that could be used to support the army; resolutely he had the will to destroy the bandits, and often spoke of it with his fellow officials.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiantai feared his homeland would be ravaged; his family was wealthy enough to feed troops, and he burned with resolve to crush the rebels, saying so often to his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 會平陽陷，帝臨朝嘆曰：「朕非亡國之君，事事皆亡國之象。

translations.literal: When Pingyang fell, the emperor at court sighed and said: "I am not a monarch who loses a state, yet in everything there are signs of a state lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingyang fell, the emperor lamented at court, "I am no destined ruin of a dynasty, yet every omen says the dynasty is falling.

sentences.zh: 祖宗櫛風沐雨之天下，一朝失之，何面目見於地下！

translations.literal: The realm our ancestors won through wind and rain—lost in a morning—what face have I to meet them underground!
translations.idiomatic: The empire our forebears won through hardship—gone in a morning—what face shall I show them in the grave!

sentences.zh: 朕願督師親決一戰，身死沙場無所恨，但死不瞑目耳！」

translations.literal: I wish to supervise the army and personally decide one battle; to die on the battlefield I have no regret, but I would die with eyes unclosed!"
translations.idiomatic: I would take command myself and fight one decisive battle; I would not regret dying on the field, but I would die with my eyes still open!"

sentences.zh: 語畢痛哭。

translations.literal: When the words ended he wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into bitter weeping as he finished.

sentences.zh: 陳演、蔣德璟諸輔臣請代，俱不許。

translations.literal: Chen Yan, Jiang Dejing, and the other chief ministers asked to go in his stead; all were refused.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan, Jiang Dejing, and the other grand secretaries volunteered to go in his place; the emperor refused them all.

sentences.zh: 建泰頓首曰：「臣家曲沃，願出私財餉軍，不煩官帑，請提師以西。」

translations.literal: Jiantai bowed his head and said: "My family is in Quwo; I wish to bring out private wealth to provision the army without troubling the public coffers, and ask to lead troops westward."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiantai kowtowed and said, "My home is Quwo; I will supply the army from my own purse without touching the treasury—let me lead troops west."

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，慰勞再三，曰：「卿若行，朕仿古推轂禮。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, comforted and encouraged him again and again, saying: "If you go, I will follow the ancient rite of pushing the chariot."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed, praising him again and again: "If you march, I will honor you with the ancient rite of sending a general to war."

sentences.zh: 建泰退，即請復故御史衛楨固官；

translations.literal: Jiantai withdrew and immediately asked to restore former censor Wei Zhen to office;
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiantai withdrew and at once asked that the former censor Wei Zhen be restored to office;

sentences.zh: 授進士淩駉職方主事，並監軍；

translations.literal: he appointed jinshi Ling Ting as Director of the Bureau of Appointments and also army supervisor;
translations.idiomatic: he named the jinshi Ling Ting Director of the Bureau of Appointments and army supervisor;

sentences.zh: 參將郭中傑為副總兵，領中軍事；

translations.literal: Regimental Commander Guo Zhongjie was made vice commander-in-chief to lead central army affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Regimental Commander Guo Zhongjie was made deputy commander-in-chief in charge of the central army;

sentences.zh: 薦進士石釭聯絡延、寧、甘、固義士，討賊立功。

translations.literal: he recommended jinshi Shi Gang to rally loyal men of Yan, Ning, Gan, and Gu to attack bandits and win merit.
translations.idiomatic: he recommended the jinshi Shi Gang to rally loyalists in Yan, Ning, Gan, and Gu to strike the rebels and earn glory.

sentences.zh: 帝俱從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented to all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every appointment.

sentences.zh: 加建泰兵部尚書，賜尚方劍，便宜從事。

translations.literal: Jiantai was promoted to Minister of War and given the Imperial Sword to act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiantai was made Minister of War and granted the Imperial Sword to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 二十六日，行遣將禮。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day the rite of dispatching the general was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth the court held the rite of dispatching the commander.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉萬煒以特牲告太廟。

translations.literal: Chief Commandant of the Horse Wan Wei offered special sacrificial beasts to announce at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Commandant of the Horse Wan Wei offered sacrificial oxen at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 日將午，帝御正陽門樓，衛士東西列，自午門抵城外，旌旗甲仗甚設。

translations.literal: Near noon the emperor ascended the Zhengyang Gate tower; guards stood east and west in ranks from the Meridian Gate to outside the city, with banners, flags, and armor grandly displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Near noon the emperor took the Zhengyang Gate tower; guards lined east and west from the Meridian Gate to beyond the walls, banners and armor in full array.

sentences.zh: 內閣五府六部都察院掌印官及京營文武大臣侍立，鴻臚贊禮，御史糾儀。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries, the Five Offices, Six Ministries, Censorate seal-holders, and capital military civil and martial ministers stood in attendance; the Court of Imperial Entertainments intoned the rites and censors corrected protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries, heads of the Five Offices and Six Ministries, Censorate chiefs, and capital military commanders stood by; the Court of Imperial Entertainments led the ceremony while censors enforced decorum.

sentences.zh: 建泰前致辭，帝獎勞有加，賜之宴。

translations.literal: Jiantai stepped forward to speak his farewell; the emperor praised and comforted him abundantly and granted a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiantai stepped forward with parting words; the emperor heaped praise upon him and ordered a feast.

sentences.zh: 禦席居中，諸臣陪侍，酒七行，帝手金卮親酌建泰者三，即以賜之，乃出手敕曰「代朕親征」。

translations.literal: The imperial seat was centered; the various ministers attended; after seven rounds of wine the emperor thrice personally poured from a golden goblet for Jiantai and then bestowed it on him, and produced a hand edict saying "Campaign in my stead."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sat at the center with ministers attending; after seven rounds he thrice poured from a golden cup for Li Jiantai with his own hand, gifted him the cup, and issued a personal edict: "Fight as my proxy."

sentences.zh: 宴畢，內臣為披紅簪花，用鼓樂導尚方劍而出。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, inner eunuchs draped red and pinned flowers; with drum and music they escorted the Imperial Sword out.
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended, palace eunuchs robed him in red and pinned victory flowers; drums and music led the Imperial Sword out of the gate.

sentences.zh: 建泰頓首謝，且辭行，帝目送之。

translations.literal: Jiantai bowed his head in thanks and took leave to depart; the emperor watched him go.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiantai kowtowed in thanks and set out; the emperor watched until he was gone.

sentences.zh: 行數里，所乘肩輿忽折，眾以為不祥。

translations.literal: After traveling several li, the sedan chair he rode suddenly broke; the crowd took it as ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: A few li from the city the sedan chair he rode snapped in two; onlookers read it as a dire omen.

sentences.zh: 建泰以宰輔督師，兵食並絀，所攜止五百人。

translations.literal: Jiantai, as chief minister supervising the army, found troops and provisions both short; what he brought amounted to only five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: As a grand secretary turned field commander, Li Jiantai had too few troops and too little grain—only five hundred men followed him.

sentences.zh: 甫出都，聞曲沃已破，家貲盡沒，驚怛而病。

translations.literal: Just after leaving the capital he heard Quwo had already fallen and family wealth was entirely lost; shocked and anguished, he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Barely out of Beijing he learned Quwo had fallen and his family fortune was gone; shock and grief laid him low.

sentences.zh: 日行三十里，士卒多道亡。

translations.literal: Each day he traveled thirty li; soldiers mostly deserted on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He managed thirty li a day while his soldiers melted away on the march.

sentences.zh: 至定興，城門閉不納。

translations.literal: Arriving at Dingxing, the city gates were closed and would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: At Dingxing the gates were shut against him.

sentences.zh: 留三日，攻破之，笞其長吏。

translations.literal: He stayed three days, then stormed and broke it open and flogged its chief official.
translations.idiomatic: After three days he forced the gates, entered, and flogged the local magistrate.

sentences.zh: 抵保定，賊鋒已逼，不敢前，入屯城中。

translations.literal: Reaching Baoding, the bandit spearhead already pressed close; he dared not advance and entered to garrison within the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Baoding the rebel vanguard was already near; he dared not march on and holed up inside the city.

sentences.zh: 已而城陷，知府何復、鄉官張羅彥等並死之。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; Prefect He Fu, local gentry leader Zhang Luoyan, and others all died for the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell; Prefect He Fu, the local leader Zhang Luoyan, and others died defending it.

sentences.zh: 建泰自刎不殊，為賊將劉方亮所執，送賊所。

translations.literal: Jiantai cut his own throat but did not die; he was seized by the bandit general Liu Fangliang and sent to the bandit headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiantai tried to cut his throat but survived; the rebel general Liu Fangliang seized him and sent him to the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 賊既敗，大清召為內院大學士。

translations.literal: After the bandits were defeated, the Great Qing summoned him as Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were broken, the Qing summoned him as a Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷歸。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 姜襄反大同，建泰遙應之。

translations.literal: When Jiang Xiang rebelled at Datong, Jiantai responded from afar in sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Xiang rose in Datong, Li Jiantai lent support from afar.

sentences.zh: 兵敗被擒，伏誅。

translations.literal: When troops were defeated he was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: When his forces were crushed he was captured and put to death.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：天下治亂，系於宰輔。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The ordering of peace and chaos under Heaven hangs on the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Whether the realm knows order or chaos hangs on its chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 自溫體仁導帝以刻深，治尚操切，由是接踵一跡。

translations.literal: From the time Wen Tiren led the emperor toward severity, governance prized harsh control, and from this ministers followed in one track.
translations.idiomatic: From Wen Tiren onward the emperor was steered toward severity; government prized harsh control, and minister after minister walked the same path.

sentences.zh: 應熊剛很，至發險忮。

translations.literal: Yingxiong was obstinate and harsh, Zhifa crafty and jealous.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yingxiong was rigid and brutal; Chen Zhifa was treacherous and jealous.

sentences.zh: 國觀陰鷙，一效體仁之所為，而國家之元氣已索然殆盡矣。

translations.literal: Guo Guan was dark and ruthless, copying all that Tiren had done, and the nation's vital force was already bleakly nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Guo'an was secretive and cruel, mimicking Wen Tiren in everything, until the dynasty's vital breath was all but spent.

sentences.zh: 至於演、藻德之徒，機智弗如，而庸庸益甚，禍中於國，旋及其身，悲夫！

translations.literal: As for men like Yan and Zaode, less clever by far and yet even more mediocre, calamity struck the state and swiftly reached themselves—lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Men like Chen Yan and Wei Zaode were less cunning still and even more feckless; disaster swallowed the realm and quickly swallowed them too—how lamentable!
